Scorpio encourages commitment to the things that genuinely matter, making this a meaningful time to consider what you want to nurture and what needs to change for that growth to happen.
✦ This month invites you to...
✨ Turn a personal realisation into a choice you can live by.
✨ Welcome relationships that make honesty and mutual care feel natural.
✨ Give a meaningful ambition the courage and attention it deserves.
✨ Explore an idea that opens your world to fresh possibilities.
✨ Create practical habits that help your dreams become part of everyday life.
An important moment of understanding arrives on 4 November, when the Sun meets Mercury retrograde in Scorpio. This Mercury cazimi brings a symbolic point of illumination within the retrograde journey, helping a conversation, memory or overlooked detail take on new meaning. Something you have been trying to explain may finally find its words. Give yourself space to record what becomes clear, allowing the insight to develop before deciding what it means for your next move.
The New Moon in Scorpio follows on 9 November, opening a lunar cycle centred around personal transformation, trust and deeper commitment. With Mercury and Venus still retrograde, a new intention may grow from something you have already been reconsidering. You could return to a meaningful desire with a clearer understanding of what it requires from you. This is a lovely opportunity to choose a beginning that feels honest, including the changes in your own behaviour that will help support it.
The middle of the month brings two significant turning points. Mercury stations direct in Scorpio on 13 November, beginning a gradual shift within communication, decisions and plans that have required revision. Answers may emerge in stages as unfinished discussions resume and missing information becomes available. Use what you have learned to ask clearer questions and approach an earlier decision with greater understanding.
Venus stations direct in Libra on 14 November, bringing love, self-worth, pleasure and personal values towards a new phase of expression. You may become more comfortable with a preference you previously questioned or recognise how you want a relationship to feel in everyday life. Both planets move slowly around their stations, so give developments time to settle. Their forward movement offers opportunities to practise the standards and priorities you have been discovering.
Confidence builds as Mars meets Jupiter in Leo on 16 November. This expressive combination brings courage, creative ambition and a desire to participate more fully in the opportunities around you. A personal project, leadership role or chance to share your talents may feel particularly exciting. Let yourself enjoy that enthusiasm while checking the preparation and responsibilities involved, giving a bold idea enough support to develop beyond its first burst of energy.
The days that follow ask us to handle that momentum thoughtfully. The Sun’s squares to Jupiter and Mars can amplify impatience, expectations and the urge to prove ourselves. A promising opportunity may look larger than it is, or a small disagreement could become more heated than anyone intended. Keep your choices connected to the result you genuinely want, with enough room to check details and recognise when your energy needs a gentler pace.
The atmosphere opens out when the Sun enters Sagittarius on 22 November. Learning, travel, discovery and the beliefs shaping our future become more prominent. You may feel curious about an experience you have kept on your wish list or ready to question an assumption about what is available to you. Sagittarius season encourages us to follow those questions, gathering knowledge that helps a larger possibility feel closer and more achievable.
The Full Moon in Gemini arrives on 24 November, bringing communication, information and personal stories to a revealing point. Close to Uranus, this lunation may coincide with unexpected news or a sudden change in perspective. A conversation, course or piece of writing could reach an important stage, showing you how much your understanding has developed. Allow time to absorb what emerges and give yourself permission to update an opinion when the evidence changes.
Mars enters Virgo late on 25 November, beginning a more practical chapter in how we pursue our goals. Attention turns towards skills, routines and the small details that make an idea usable. You may feel motivated to practise, repair or improve something that has repeatedly slowed you down. Keep your standards supportive and choose an approach you can maintain, allowing competence to grow through experience.
The final days of November bring opportunities to combine enjoyment with thoughtful progress. Venus’s close connection with Jupiter encourages warmth and generosity, while the Sun’s approaching trine with Saturn supports patience and reliable effort. The Uranus–Pluto trine also reaches exactness on 29 November, highlighting a longer-term period of innovation involving ideas, technology and communities. Consider which changes genuinely help you participate in the future you want to create.
November is ultimately a month of allowing your discoveries to influence how you live. You may leave it with clearer preferences, a more honest conversation behind you or an ambition that finally has a practical next step. Give yourself credit for those developments and enjoy the possibilities they bring. There is something wonderfully encouraging about moving forwards with a better understanding of yourself and choosing a direction that feels increasingly your own.

December carries a beautiful mixture of dreaming, reviewing and building. The month begins with plenty of Sagittarius energy, encouraging you to look beyond your current circumstances and reconnect with possibility. Curiosity returns, ideas grow and the future may feel wider than it has for a while. There is a desire to learn, explore and believe in something bigger, although Mercury’s tense conversations with Mars and Uranus suggest that enthusiasm needs patience. Plans may change quickly, conversations could become reactive and unexpected information may ask you to reconsider what you thought you knew.

The Sagittarius New Moon on 9 December opens a fresh chapter around growth, adventure, faith and personal truth. This is a powerful moment to plant intentions connected to experiences you want to have and the person you are becoming. Sagittarius wants movement and expansion, so intentions will benefit from including a real-world action rather than remaining beautiful ideas. The invitation is to choose a direction that genuinely excites you, then take the first brave step without demanding the entire route in advance.

The middle of the month marks a major energetic shift. Saturn turns direct in Aries on 10 December, followed by Neptune turning direct in Aries on 12 December. Dreams that have felt uncertain since the summer may begin asking for courage, boundaries and practical commitment. You may understand more clearly which visions still feel alive and which ones belonged to an earlier version of you. Progress may remain gradual, but the internal pause begins to lift and decisions can feel easier to trust.

Jupiter turns retrograde in Leo on 13 December, beginning a review of confidence, visibility, creativity and joy. This is not a retreat from expansion. It is an opportunity to reconnect with what makes success meaningful to you personally. You may revisit an ambition, creative project or desire for recognition and realise that it needs to feel more authentic. The second half of December supports refining the dream so that it reflects who you are now, rather than who you once thought you needed to become.

As the Sun enters Capricorn on 21 December, the atmosphere becomes more focused and intentional. Big Sagittarius visions begin asking for structure, timelines and sustainable foundations. This shift can be incredibly motivating, although tense connections to Saturn and Neptune remind you to balance ambition with realistic capacity. You do not need to build the whole future before the year ends. One thoughtful decision or well-supported next step can carry far more power than an overwhelming list of resolutions.

The Cancer Full Moon on 24 December brings emotions, home, family, belonging and personal needs into the spotlight. Feelings may rise quickly, especially around old roles or responsibilities. This lunation offers an opportunity to recognise where you have created greater emotional safety since July and where stronger boundaries are still needed. Care is a central theme, including the care you offer yourself when familiar dynamics become demanding.

Mercury enters Capricorn on 25 December, helping you organise recent insights into clearer plans. The final week of the year is practical and reflective, with supportive connections to Mars encouraging action while Saturn asks for maturity and patience. There may be moments of self-doubt or pressure, but this energy is ultimately helping you distinguish between goals that inspire you and obligations that simply exhaust you.

December closes beneath a Third Quarter Moon in Libra, bringing the year to an end with questions of balance, reciprocity and alignment. The final days are well suited to reviewing what deserves to continue, what needs adjusting and what you are ready to leave behind. There is no need to reinvent yourself overnight. The most powerful way to enter 2027 is with a clearer understanding of your values, your capacity and the future you genuinely want to create.

✦ December’s Main Themes

✦ Reconnecting with possibility and choosing a new direction
✦ Giving dreams practical foundations
✦ Reviewing confidence, creativity and the desire to be seen
✦ Creating stronger emotional safety and healthier boundaries
✦ Releasing goals and responsibilities that no longer feel aligned
✦ Entering 2027 with intention rather than pressure  

December invites you to dream widely, choose carefully and build gently. Let the month show you which visions still create a spark within you, then give those visions the time, structure and devotion they need to become real.

beyond.intro: A reference to the planets, signs and houses, and what they could mean beyond the everyday: past lives, hidden gifts and the occult. Each page explains the placement in plain language, and where it has been written, adds a past-life view and a hidden-chart view.
beyond.note: Past-life and hidden-chart readings are traditions and a lens for reflection, not facts.

groups.name: Planets
groups.blurb: The ten bodies and what each one does.

items.name: The Sun
items.summary: Your core self, your life force and what you are growing into.
basics: The Sun is the centre of the chart, just as it is the centre of the solar system. It shows your core identity: the self you are growing into, the way you shine and what makes you feel most alive. It rules Leo, and it takes about a year to travel through the whole zodiac, spending roughly a month in each sign. That is why your Sun sign is the one most people know.

It helps to see the Sun as a purpose and not a personality. Your Moon, Mercury and Venus describe how you feel, think and love. Your Sun describes what you are here to become, and the part of you that feels most like you when you are doing well.
## What it governs
Identity, vitality, willpower, confidence, creative expression, the father and father figures, leadership, and the sense of having a purpose.
## At its best
A strong, well used Sun is warm, generous and clear about who it is. You can stand in the light without needing to be applauded, and you can let other people shine too.
## When it is hard

A struggling Sun can feel invisible, doubtful or overshadowed, or it can swing the other way into pride, a need to be the centre or a fear of being ordinary. Both come from the same place: not yet trusting that you are enough as you are.
## Finding it in your chart

Look for the Sun glyph, a circle with a dot in the middle. Its sign is the style of your identity. Its house is the area of life where you most want to be seen and where you grow into yourself. The aspects it makes show which other parts of you it works with or against.
## The Sun through the signs
* Aries: Direct and brave. You grow by starting things, leading and being honest about what you want.
* Taurus: Steady and grounded. You grow by building something lasting and enjoying the real, physical world.
* Gemini: Curious and quick. You grow by learning, talking and following your many interests.
* Cancer: Caring and protective. You grow by nurturing, by making a home, and by trusting your feelings.
* Leo: Warm and expressive. You grow by creating, by loving openly and by taking your place in the light.
* Virgo: Practical and thoughtful. You grow by being useful, by refining things and by caring for details.
* Libra: Gracious and fair. You grow through relationship, beauty and finding the balance between two sides.
* Scorpio: Intense and deep. You grow through facing what is hidden and through change that goes to the root.
* Sagittarius: Free and honest. You grow by exploring, by seeking truth and by following a bigger meaning.
* Capricorn: Ambitious and disciplined. You grow by building towards a goal and by earning your authority.
* Aquarius: Original and independent. You grow by being yourself, by thinking ahead and by serving a larger group.
* Pisces: Gentle and imaginative. You grow through compassion, creativity and listening to your inner world.
## The Sun through the houses
* 1st house: Your identity is front and centre. You are strongly yourself and often noticed.
* 2nd house: You find your purpose through what you value, your talents and how you earn.
* 3rd house: You shine through communication, learning, writing and your close circle.
* 4th house: Home, family and your roots are the heart of who you are.
* 5th house: You come alive through creativity, romance, play and children.
* 6th house: You find purpose in work, craft, service and looking after your wellbeing.
* 7th house: You discover yourself through partnership and one to one relationships.
* 8th house: You are drawn to depth, to intimacy, to shared resources and to transformation.
* 9th house: Your purpose grows through learning, travel, teaching and belief.
* 10th house: Your calling is public. Career and reputation matter to who you are.
* 11th house: You shine in groups, friendships and shared hopes for the future.
* 12th house: Your purpose works quietly. Solitude, spirituality and the hidden matter to you.
past: In past-life astrology, the Sun is the part of you that is ready to be seen in this lifetime. Where the Moon and the nodes are read as memory, the Sun is read as intention: what you came to express, and what you may have held back before.
## Stories it may point to

A Sun that feels shy, blocked or overshadowed is often read as a sign of lives spent in the background, serving someone else's purpose or keeping your head down to stay safe. A very bright, confident Sun can point to lives of leadership, performance or visibility, with the lesson now being humility and shared light.

The Sun's house shows where that story is being worked on. A Sun in the twelfth house, for example, is sometimes read as a soul that lived much of its power out of sight, and is now learning to step forward at its own pace.
## The lesson
To let yourself be seen, and to know that you are allowed to take up space. For the proud Sun, the lesson is the reverse: to share the light and to be loved without having to perform.
## Questions to sit with
* When do I feel most like myself?
* Where do I hide, and who taught me that hiding was safer?
* What would I do this year if I knew I would be supported?

items.name: The Moon
items.summary: Your feelings, instincts and need for safety.
basics: The Moon is the second most important body in the chart. It shows your emotional world: how you feel, what you need to feel safe and how you comfort yourself. It rules Cancer and moves faster than anything else, spending about two and a half days in each sign and circling the whole zodiac in under a month.

Where the Sun is who you are becoming, the Moon is who you already are underneath. It is habit, instinct, memory and mood. It is also closely linked with home, with the mother or the person who first cared for you, and with the body and its rhythms.
## What it governs
Emotions, instincts, habits, comfort, nurture, memory, the home, the mother and mother figures, the body and its cycles, and your private self.
## At its best
A well supported Moon is emotionally honest and responsive. You know what you feel, you can ask for what you need, and you can offer others a feeling of safety.
## When it is hard
A troubled Moon can mean moods that swing, old hurts that return, clinging, withdrawing or finding it hard to name what you feel. Often it is simply a part of you that has not yet been soothed.
## Finding it in your chart

The Moon glyph is a crescent. Because the Moon moves so fast, you need your birth time to be sure of its sign if you were born near a change. Its sign is your emotional style, and its house is where you look for security.
## The Moon through the signs
* Aries: Feelings come fast and are expressed directly. You need independence and action, and you recover quickly.
* Taurus: You feel safest with comfort, routine and the senses. Change unsettles you, and loyalty runs deep.
* Gemini: You process feelings by talking and thinking. You need variety, and you can be restless.
* Cancer: Very sensitive and protective. Home and family matter hugely, and you feel everything in the room.
* Leo: You need warmth, appreciation and to be loved openly. You feel generously and want to be seen.
* Virgo: You feel safe when things are in order and useful. You can worry, and you show love by helping.
* Libra: You need harmony and company, and you dislike conflict. You feel balanced when you are in relationship.
* Scorpio: Deep, private and intense. You feel strongly and keep much hidden, and you do not forget.
* Sagittarius: You need freedom, space and meaning. You feel hopeful and restless, and you lighten others' moods.
* Capricorn: Reserved and self controlled. You feel safe when you are competent, and you can find it hard to show need.
* Aquarius: You need independence and a little distance. You feel for the group, and can be detached about your own feelings.
* Pisces: Open, absorbent and deeply empathic. You feel the moods of others and need time alone to recover.
## The Moon through the houses
* 1st house: Your feelings show on your face. You react quickly and others read your moods easily.
* 2nd house: You feel secure through money, possessions and having your own resources.
* 3rd house: You feel through talking, writing and your closest circle. Siblings and neighbours matter.
* 4th house: Home is your emotional base. You need a place that feels safe and your family ties are strong.
* 5th house: You feel through creativity, romance and play. You need joy to feel well.
* 6th house: You feel better with routine and meaningful work, and stress can show in your body.
* 7th house: You need closeness. You feel secure through partnership and mirror your partners' moods.
* 8th house: Your emotions run deep. You are drawn to intimacy, to secrets and to emotional transformation.
* 9th house: You feel at home when you are learning, travelling or exploring what you believe.
* 10th house: Your feelings are tied to your public role. You may be drawn to caring or nurturing work.
* 11th house: You find emotional safety among friends and groups, and in shared hopes.
* 12th house: You feel a lot in private. You need solitude, rest and quiet to restore yourself.
past: The Moon is often read as your emotional memory. It carries the feelings, habits and attachments that seem older than this lifetime: reactions that feel out of proportion, a deep pull to a certain place or person, or a sense of knowing something you have no reason to know.
## Stories it may point to

The Moon's sign is read as the emotional climate you grew used to: a Moon in a water sign, for example, is sometimes linked with lives in which feeling deeply was both a gift and a danger. A Moon in an earth sign may point to lives where safety came from land, craft and routine. The Moon's house shows where those old feelings are most active.
It can also point to who you were close to: family bonds, a mother, a child, or a community that felt like home. People with a strong Moon often describe an old tie to a place, a song or a face.
## The lesson
To meet your own needs and to let old feelings be felt, not carried. The Moon asks you to become your own safe place.
## Moon through the signs, as a past-life theme
* Aries: Old habits of self reliance and of fighting for your own safety. The lesson is to be gentle and to let others help.
* Taurus: A deep need for security and comfort, perhaps from lives of scarcity. The lesson is to trust that you will be provided for.
* Gemini: Lives of words, messages and many connections. The lesson is to slow down and to feel, not only to think.
* Cancer: Strong family and mothering memories. The lesson is to protect without smothering, and to let go.
* Leo: Lives of being admired, or of not being seen. The lesson is to feel loved without having to perform.
* Virgo: Lives of service and of being needed. The lesson is to accept that you are enough, and to rest.
* Libra: Lives shaped by partnership and keeping the peace. The lesson is to name your own needs.
* Scorpio: Lives of intense loyalty, loss and secrets. The lesson is to trust again and to let feelings move.
* Sagittarius: Lives of wandering and of faith. The lesson is to feel at home wherever you are.
* Capricorn: Lives of duty and of having to be strong. The lesson is to allow yourself to need care.
* Aquarius: Lives as an outsider or among a group. The lesson is to let people close.
* Pisces: Lives of devotion, sacrifice or retreat. The lesson is to protect your own boundaries.
## Questions to sit with
* Which of my feelings seems older than I am?
* What did I need as a child that I can give myself now?
* Which place or person feels like home to me, and why?
hidden: The Moon is the traditional planet of dreams, intuition and the unseen. In the hidden chart she is the ruler of the inner life: what you sense before you can explain it, and the tides of the month that many people feel in their own body and mood.
## In practice

Many people with a strong or prominent Moon work with the phases: setting intentions at the new moon, releasing at the dark moon and gathering at the full moon. Others keep a dream journal, read tarot by moonlight or find that their sleep and emotions follow the lunar cycle closely.

A watery Moon (Cancer, Scorpio or Pisces) is often linked with strong intuition. An airy or earthy Moon can be just as sensitive, but may need a practice, such as writing, walking or ritual, to hear it.

items.name: Mercury
items.summary: How you think, learn and communicate.
basics: Mercury is the messenger. It shows how your mind works: how you think, talk, write, learn and make connections. It rules Gemini and Virgo and never strays far from the Sun, so it is always in your Sun sign or in one of the signs on either side of it.
Mercury is what you notice, what you remember and how you put it into words. Two people with the same Sun can think completely differently if their Mercury is in different signs.
## What it governs
Thought, speech, writing, learning, curiosity, short journeys, siblings, neighbours, trade, technology and everyday contact with other people.
## At its best
A well used Mercury is curious, clear and quick to understand. You can explain things, listen well and see how two ideas connect.
## When it is hard

Mercury can go to overthinking, nervous chatter, scattered attention or words that come out wrong. When it is retrograde, many people notice the same themes returning, as old conversations and ideas come back for another look.
## Finding it in your chart
The glyph is a circle with a crescent above and a cross below. Its sign is the style of your mind, and its house is where you talk, learn and exchange ideas.
## Mercury through the signs
* Aries: Fast, direct and blunt. You think on your feet and say what you mean.
* Taurus: Slow, steady and practical. You take time to decide, and then you rarely change your mind.
* Gemini: Quick, curious and talkative. You collect information and like to connect ideas.
* Cancer: Intuitive and feeling. You think through memory and mood, and remember how things felt.
* Leo: Confident and dramatic. You speak with warmth and like a story with a flourish.
* Virgo: Precise, analytical and observant. You notice details and like to improve things.
* Libra: Balanced and diplomatic. You weigh both sides and think best in conversation.
* Scorpio: Deep, probing and private. You look beneath the surface and keep your thoughts to yourself.
* Sagittarius: Big picture and honest. You think in ideas and principles and love to learn about the world.
* Capricorn: Structured and serious. You think in plans and facts and prefer to be useful.
* Aquarius: Original and inventive. You think in systems and ideas that are ahead of their time.
* Pisces: Imaginative and absorbing. You think in images, hunches and feelings, and may find it hard to put into words.
## Mercury through the houses
* 1st house: Your mind shows in the way you present yourself. You come across as quick and expressive.
* 2nd house: You think about money and value. Your voice and your skills may earn your living.
* 3rd house: A natural place for Mercury. You are curious and talkative, and siblings and neighbours matter.
* 4th house: You think and talk about home and family, and you may work from home.
* 5th house: You express ideas through creativity, humour, romance and play.
* 6th house: Your mind is busy with work and routines. You are good at analysing and fixing things.
* 7th house: You think best in dialogue. Partners are often also your closest conversation.
* 8th house: Your mind is drawn to secrets, psychology and what lies beneath the surface.
* 9th house: You love to study, to travel and to explore big ideas, and you may teach or write.
* 10th house: Your reputation rests on what you say. You may work with words or communication.
* 11th house: You think among friends and groups, and are drawn to shared ideas and causes.
* 12th house: Much of your thinking is private and unspoken. You have a rich inner world and a strong intuition.
past: In past-life astrology, Mercury suggests the skills of mind and voice you bring with you. Languages, writing and teaching that come easily may be read as practice from earlier lives, and so may a sense of having been a messenger, a trader or a scribe.
## Stories it may point to

A fluent, quick Mercury often goes with the idea of lives spent among words: storytellers, scholars, couriers. A hard or silent Mercury is sometimes read as lives in which you were not heard, were silenced or had to hide what you knew. People with this often find that putting thoughts into words, in writing or aloud, feels unusually charged.
Mercury retrograde at birth is often read as unfinished conversations: a message you did not get to say, or a lesson you are meant to explain in a new way.
## The lesson
To trust your voice and to speak and write what is true for you. If words come easily, to use them kindly and to listen as well as you speak.
## Questions to sit with
* What have I always been able to explain, without being taught?
* What do I find hard to say, and what is that about?
* If my voice were safe, what would I say?
hidden: Mercury is the god of messages and crossings, and the traditional guide between worlds. In the hidden chart he is the planet of languages, symbols and codes: the part of you that can read a tarot spread, learn a system of correspondences or notice a pattern between two ideas.
## In practice

A strong Mercury is often drawn to the study side of the occult: sigils, alphabets, divination systems and writing down what comes. Journalling, spoken spells and written intentions all sit well with it.

items.name: Venus
items.summary: What you love, value and are drawn to.
basics: Venus shows what you love and what you value. It governs attraction, beauty, pleasure, friendship, money and how you connect. It rules Taurus and Libra, and like Mercury it stays close to the Sun, so it is always in your Sun sign or within two signs of it.
Your Venus describes how you give and receive love, what you find beautiful, and what you are willing to spend your time and money on. It is also about self worth: how much you feel you deserve.
## What it governs
Love, attraction, relationships, harmony, beauty, art, pleasure, money, values, friendship and the things you are drawn to.
## At its best
A well supported Venus is affectionate, gracious and at ease with pleasure. You know what you like, you can give and receive love freely and you bring beauty and peace into the space around you.
## When it is hard
Venus can go into people pleasing, jealousy, overspending, avoiding conflict or putting your worth in what others think. It is often a question of value: do you believe you are worth what you want?
## Finding it in your chart
The glyph is a circle with a cross beneath it. Its sign is your style of loving and your taste, and its house is where you seek harmony and enjoyment.
## Venus through the signs
* Aries: You love directly and with passion. You like the chase and need independence in love.
* Taurus: Loyal, sensual and steady. You love through touch, time and loyalty, and you value comfort.
* Gemini: Playful and curious. You love through words and fun, and you need variety and conversation.
* Cancer: Tender and protective. You love by caring and by making a home, and you need emotional safety.
* Leo: Warm, generous and dramatic. You love with your whole heart and want to be adored in return.
* Virgo: Modest and devoted. You love by serving and noticing, and you may be shy about showing it.
* Libra: Charming and romantic. You love beauty and partnership, and you are at home in Libra.
* Scorpio: Intense, loyal and private. You love deeply, all or nothing, and you value truth and trust.
* Sagittarius: Free and adventurous. You love openness and humour, and you need room to roam.
* Capricorn: Serious and committed. You love slowly and for the long term, and you show it through reliability.
* Aquarius: Independent and unconventional. You love friendship first, and you value freedom and originality.
* Pisces: Dreamy and compassionate. You love unconditionally, sometimes too much, and you are drawn to the ideal.
## Venus through the houses
* 1st house: You are charming and attractive. Others are drawn to your presence.
* 2nd house: You love beautiful things and feel secure with money. You often have a gift for earning through art or beauty.
* 3rd house: You are sweet spoken and enjoy friendly company, writing and your close circle.
* 4th house: You love a beautiful, peaceful home, and family is a source of love.
* 5th house: A joyful placement. You love romance, art, children and play.
* 6th house: You show love through service, and you may find pleasure in your work and your routines.
* 7th house: A natural place for Venus. You value partnership and are drawn to romance and cooperation.
* 8th house: You love intensely and are drawn to deep bonds, shared resources and transformation through love.
* 9th house: You love freedom, travel and learning, and may meet partners through other cultures or beliefs.
* 10th house: You are liked in public life and may work in art, beauty or diplomacy.
* 11th house: You are loved by friends and groups, and often find love through friendship.
* 12th house: Your love can be private or secret. You are drawn to compassion, spirituality and the hidden side of love.
past: Venus is read as a record of how you have loved and what you have prized. Your tastes, the people you are drawn to and the lessons you have about worth are all linked to her in this tradition.
## Stories it may point to

A strong attraction on first meeting someone, an old taste for a certain kind of art, place or era, or a pattern of falling for the same type of person are all things that people with a prominent Venus describe. In past-life astrology these are sometimes read as old bonds and old loves recognising each other again.

Venus in a hard aspect or in the twelfth house is sometimes read as love that was hidden, forbidden or lost, and lessons about self worth that carry on. A harmonious Venus may point to lives in which love and beauty were freely given.
## The lesson
To value yourself without needing to earn it, and to love without losing yourself. Venus asks you to know your own worth.
## Questions to sit with
* What kind of love do I keep looking for, and where did I learn it?
* Do I give love in order to be loved back?
* What do I truly value, and how does my life show it?
hidden: Venus is the goddess of love and beauty, and in the hidden chart she rules attraction as a kind of magic: glamour, charm, the drawing power of intention. She is the planet of love spells in folklore and of the arts of pleasure and adornment.
## In practice

People with a prominent Venus often work with beauty as ritual: flowers, perfumes, candles, altars, making a space lovely so that it holds a mood. She is also linked with self love practices and with the work of knowing what you truly want.

items.name: Mars
basics: Mars is the planet of energy and action. It shows how you go after what you want, how you assert yourself and how you protect yourself. It rules Aries and, in the traditional system, Scorpio too. It spends about six weeks in each sign and takes roughly two years to travel the whole zodiac.
Mars is the fire in the body: appetite, anger, drive, courage and sexual desire. Without it, nothing starts. With too much, you can find yourself pushing, fighting or burning out.
## What it governs
Drive, ambition, action, courage, desire, anger, competition, sport, the body, surgery and defence.
## At its best
A well used Mars is brave and decisive. You can stand up for yourself and others, start what needs starting and put energy into what matters without harming anyone.
## When it is hard
A difficult Mars can mean a short temper, impatience, picking fights, or the opposite: swallowed anger, passivity and burnout from not acting. Learning to use anger as information is a common task.
## Finding it in your chart
The glyph is a circle with an arrow pointing up and to the right. Its sign is your style of action, and its house is where you spend your energy and where you are most likely to meet a challenge.
## Mars through the signs
* Aries: At home here. Bold, fast and competitive. You act first and need a challenge.
* Taurus: Steady and stubborn. Slow to start but very hard to stop. You act when you are sure.
* Gemini: Quick, restless and verbal. You act through words and ideas, and you can scatter your energy.
* Cancer: Indirect and protective. You fight for your home and loved ones, and your moods drive your actions.
* Leo: Proud, bold and generous. You act with flair and want to lead and be admired.
* Virgo: Precise and efficient. You act through work and service, and can be critical, of yourself most of all.
* Libra: Fair minded and charming. You prefer to act through cooperation, and may avoid open conflict.
* Scorpio: Powerful, focused and strategic. You act with intensity and perseverance, and do not give up.
* Sagittarius: Adventurous and direct. You act on big ideas and need freedom, and you can be tactless.
* Capricorn: Disciplined and ambitious. You work steadily towards goals, and use your energy well.
* Aquarius: Independent and rebellious. You act for causes and ideas, and dislike being told what to do.
* Pisces: Gentle and diffuse. You act through intuition and compassion, and find direct conflict hard.
## Mars through the houses
* 1st house: You are bold and energetic, and others see your drive straight away.
* 2nd house: You work hard for money and are protective of what you own.
* 3rd house: You are quick with words and can be argumentative. You are energetic in your everyday surroundings.
* 4th house: Energy and sometimes friction at home. You may be driven to build a secure base.
* 5th house: You pursue romance and creativity with passion, and you love competition and play.
* 6th house: You throw yourself into work and routines, and you need to avoid overwork.
* 7th house: You are drawn to strong partners, and conflicts may come through relationships.
* 8th house: Powerful and intense. You are drawn to deep bonds, shared resources and transformation.
* 9th house: You fight for beliefs and love adventure, and you may be a passionate teacher or debater.
* 10th house: You are ambitious and driven in your career, and you want to lead.
* 11th house: You are an active friend and campaigner, and take action for shared goals.
* 12th house: Your drive works behind the scenes. You may hide anger or find it hard to act openly.
past: Mars is the fighter, the protector and the pioneer. In past-life astrology he points to old patterns around anger, survival and the use of force: how you defended yourself or others, and what it cost.
## Stories it may point to

A strong Mars is often read as lives of the warrior, hunter, soldier or explorer: a body that knows how to act in danger. A suppressed Mars, or one in a hard place such as the twelfth house, may point to lives in which anger was not safe to show, or in which you were harmed and could not fight back.
These stories sometimes show up as an instant, physical reaction to conflict, a fascination with weapons or battle, or a deep fear of confrontation that seems bigger than anything in this life.
## The lesson
To use your fire to protect and to create, not to harm, and to stand up for yourself without losing yourself. For many people, the work is simply to allow anger to be felt and used.
## Questions to sit with
* How do I react when I feel threatened?
* What do I fight for, and what do I avoid fighting for?
* What would I do with my energy if I felt completely safe?
hidden: Mars is the planet of will in ritual: the drive to cut away, to banish and to protect. In the hidden chart he is linked with protective magic, the setting of boundaries and the courage it takes to work with strong energies.
## In practice

Many people with a strong Mars are drawn to physical forms of ritual, such as dance, martial arts, fire and movement, and to protection work like cleansing a space or setting a boundary. His colour is red and his metal is iron.

items.name: Jupiter
items.summary: Growth, faith and where life opens up.
basics: Jupiter is the planet of expansion. It shows where you grow, what you believe in and where life tends to feel generous. It rules Sagittarius and, in the traditional system, Pisces. It spends about a year in each sign and takes roughly twelve years to circle the zodiac, which is why people speak of a Jupiter return every twelve years.
Jupiter is the part of you that says yes, and that trusts things will work out. It is optimism, faith, wisdom and the drive to see a bigger picture.
## What it governs
Growth, opportunity, luck, abundance, optimism, belief, higher learning, teaching, travel, generosity and the search for meaning.
## At its best
A well used Jupiter is warm, wise and generous. You bring faith and humour to hard times, you learn quickly from experience and you lift people up.
## When it is hard
Too much Jupiter can mean excess, overpromising, taking more than you give, or believing that things will fix themselves. A frustrated Jupiter can feel cynical, with no sense of meaning.
## Finding it in your chart
The glyph looks like a number four, or a crescent over a cross. Its sign is the style of your optimism and what you believe in, and its house is where opportunities tend to arrive.
## Jupiter through the signs
* Aries: You grow through courage and by starting things. Your faith is in yourself.
* Taurus: You grow through patience, values and building security. You are generous with comfort.
* Gemini: You grow through learning and connecting. You are curious about everything.
* Cancer: At its strongest here. You grow through care, family and emotional wisdom.
* Leo: You grow through creativity and generosity. You are a warm, encouraging presence.
* Virgo: You grow through service and skill. You may help others with practical wisdom.
* Libra: You grow through relationship, fairness and cooperation, and you value harmony.
* Scorpio: You grow through depth, honesty and transformation. You find faith in facing what is hard.
* Sagittarius: At home here. You grow through travel, philosophy and freedom, and you are a natural optimist.
* Capricorn: You grow through discipline and long effort. You are wise about structure and success.
* Aquarius: You grow through community, originality and ideals. You believe in a better future.
* Pisces: You grow through compassion, imagination and spiritual faith.
## Jupiter through the houses
* 1st house: You are optimistic and generous, and you tend to be liked. Opportunity comes through who you are.
* 2nd house: Luck with money and resources, and a generous attitude to what you own.
* 3rd house: You love learning and ideas. You grow through writing, teaching and your close circle.
* 4th house: A happy home and a close family, and often a feeling of being protected.
* 5th house: Joy through creativity, romance and children. You are playful and enjoy life.
* 6th house: You grow through work and service, and have a good chance of finding meaningful work.
* 7th house: You are lucky in partnership and attract generous, wise people.
* 8th house: You benefit from shared resources and have a talent for transformation and healing.
* 9th house: A natural place for Jupiter. You grow through travel, study, teaching and faith.
* 10th house: Success in public life. You grow through your career and your reputation.
* 11th house: Friends and groups bring opportunity and luck, and your hopes tend to come true.
* 12th house: Quiet protection and a rich inner life, and you may be drawn to spiritual service.
past: Jupiter is read as your gifts and faith carried forward. In past-life astrology he points to where you have been generous, wise or protected, and to what you believe in so deeply that it feels like a memory.
## Stories it may point to

Lives as teachers, priests, travellers, judges and philosophers are traditionally linked with Jupiter. A strong Jupiter may point to a soul that has done good work before, and that feels naturally lucky, trusted or protected in a certain area of life.
A difficult Jupiter can suggest the opposite: lives of excess, of preaching without listening, or of faith that was shaken. The lesson then is to keep faith while staying grounded.
## The lesson
To trust the process of growth, to share what you have been given and to find meaning without needing to be right.
## Questions to sit with
* Where does life feel generous to me, and have I earned it or been given it?
* What do I truly believe, and where did it come from?
* What would I do if I trusted that I was supported?
hidden: Jupiter rules the search for meaning. In the hidden chart he is the planet of the philosophical side of magic: belief, ritual as a system, higher teachings and the wish to understand how the universe works.
## In practice

People with a prominent Jupiter are often drawn to study esoteric traditions deeply, to teach or to travel to sacred places. He is linked with abundance work, with gratitude and with ritual that celebrates and expands, such as feasts, festivals and blessings.

items.name: Saturn
items.summary: Structure, time and the lessons that take effort.
basics: Saturn is the planet of structure, limits and time. It shows where life asks for patience, responsibility and mastery. It rules Capricorn and, in the traditional system, Aquarius. It takes about two and a half years to move through a sign and about twenty-nine and a half years to circle the zodiac, which is why the Saturn return, around ages 28 to 30, is such a well known turning point.
Saturn is the teacher who makes you earn it. It rarely feels comfortable, but it builds the things that last: skill, character, boundaries and authority that is truly your own.
## What it governs
Responsibility, discipline, time, limits, structure, ambition, age, authority, fear, patience, endurance and the father or authority figures.
## At its best
A well used Saturn is reliable, wise and quietly strong. You keep your word, you build slowly and well, and others trust you. With time, Saturn becomes mastery.
## When it is hard

A heavy Saturn can bring fear, self doubt, harsh self criticism, isolation, or a sense that you must do everything alone. It can make you feel old when you are young. The way through is usually patience and self respect.
## Finding it in your chart

The glyph looks like a cross with a curved tail, often described as a scythe. Its sign is how you build authority, and its house is where you work hardest and slowly become expert. Saturn aspects to your personal planets show where responsibility weighs on you.
## Saturn through the signs
* Aries: You learn to lead and act on your own. Lessons about independence and patience, and not rushing.
* Taurus: You learn about security, money and self worth. A slow builder with strong values.
* Gemini: You learn to focus the mind and to communicate with care. Lessons about listening and depth.
* Cancer: You learn about emotional security, family and boundaries. Lessons about caring without carrying everything.
* Leo: You learn about confidence, creativity and self expression. Lessons about being seen and worthy.
* Virgo: You learn about work, health and service. A master of detail, with lessons about self criticism.
* Libra: You learn about fairness, commitment and partnership. Lessons about balance and responsibility.
* Scorpio: You learn about power, trust and intimacy. Lessons about letting go and facing fear.
* Sagittarius: You learn about belief, truth and discipline. Lessons about faith and commitment.
* Capricorn: At home here. You learn about ambition and responsibility, and build a lasting career.
* Aquarius: You learn about community, individuality and ideals. Lessons about belonging and responsibility to the group.
* Pisces: You learn about faith, boundaries and compassion. Lessons about trust and grounding.
## Saturn through the houses
* 1st house: You may feel serious or guarded. Confidence is built slowly, and you grow into your authority.
* 2nd house: Money and self worth are lessons. You build security slowly and value what you earn.
* 3rd house: You may find words hard at first and then become a careful, precise communicator.
* 4th house: Responsibilities at home or in the family. You build a strong foundation over time.
* 5th house: Joy and creativity can feel restricted at first. You learn to play, and to love without fear.
* 6th house: You are conscientious in work and health, and may work too hard. You become expert in your craft.
* 7th house: You take relationships seriously. You may marry later or meet teachers and older partners.
* 8th house: Lessons about trust, shared resources and letting go. Deep fears can become deep strength.
* 9th house: Belief and learning are things you build slowly. You may be sceptical, then wise.
* 10th house: A natural place for Saturn. You build a serious career and earn authority over time.
* 11th house: You are selective with friends, and responsible within groups. A few loyal friends matter more than many.
* 12th house: Hidden fears, solitude and old karma. Your lessons are private, and healing comes through acceptance.
past: Saturn is the great past-life planet. In this tradition he is read as unfinished lessons and old responsibilities: duties you carried, limits you were placed under, or power you once misused. His house shows where that work is still going on, and where mastery is waiting.
## Stories it may point to

Many people read Saturn as lives of hardship, duty or authority. You may have been the one in charge, with the burden of leadership, or someone held back, with the sense of being denied. Fears that are out of proportion to anything in this life, such as a fear of failure, of poverty or of being judged, are often linked to Saturn.
Saturn's sign adds the style: in a water sign the lesson is often emotional, in an earth sign material, in an air sign mental and in a fire sign about courage and self belief.
## The lesson
Saturn asks you to take responsibility for your own growth, to build patiently and to make peace with time. When you do, it becomes your greatest ally, and the fear turns into skill and authority.
## Saturn through the houses, as a past-life theme
* 1st house: An old burden of identity. You may have been made to hide or to play a role. The work is to be yourself and to trust your own authority.
* 2nd house: Old lessons of lack and of what you are worth. The work is to build security and to value yourself.
* 3rd house: Old silence or censorship. The work is to speak with care and to trust that you will be heard.
* 4th house: Old family duty or a lost home. The work is to build your own safe place and to heal ancestral patterns.
* 5th house: Old restrictions on joy and love. The work is to play again and to love without fear.
* 6th house: Lives of heavy labour or service. The work is to find dignity in work and to care for your body.
* 7th house: Old vows and difficult partnerships. The work is to commit freely and to be equal.
* 8th house: Old experiences of loss, betrayal or power. The work is to trust again and to let go.
* 9th house: Old rigid beliefs or lost faith. The work is to find your own truth and to keep an open mind.
* 10th house: Old burdens of public duty or loss of status. The work is to claim your calling with humility.
* 11th house: Old exile from the group. The work is to find your people and to belong without conforming.
* 12th house: Hidden guilt, confinement or retreat. The work is to forgive and to come out into the light.
## Questions to sit with
* What am I afraid of that does not seem to come from this life?
* Where do I feel I have to do everything alone, and why?
* What do I want to master, and what would it take?
hidden: Saturn is the old man of the zodiac and the keeper of thresholds. In the hidden chart he is linked with the discipline of magic: ritual done carefully and repeated, boundaries that protect, and the long study that turns knowledge into skill.
## In practice

People with a prominent Saturn are often drawn to the serious side of the esoteric: ceremonial work, astrology as a craft, ancestor work and the structure of a daily practice. He is also the planet of banishing and of binding, and of the protective circle. Lead is his metal, and Saturday his day.

items.name: Uranus
basics: Uranus is the planet of sudden change, originality and rebellion. It breaks patterns and brings the new. It rules Aquarius, and it was discovered in 1781, which is why it does not appear in the traditional system. It takes about seven years to move through a sign and eighty four years to circle the zodiac, so its sign marks a generation and its house is the personal part.
Uranus is the part of you that refuses to be put in a box. It is the flash of insight, the urge to be free, and the moment you decide that things cannot go on as they are.
## What it governs
Change, freedom, rebellion, invention, technology, genius, awakening, eccentricity, sudden events and the future.
## At its best
A well used Uranus is original, brave and inventive. You can see beyond the usual, break old patterns and bring in something new, for yourself and for others.
## When it is hard
Uranus can bring restlessness, instability, sudden breaks, coldness or a need to run when things get close. The task is to find freedom without leaving everyone behind.
## Finding it in your chart
The glyph looks like an H with a circle beneath, an antenna. Its sign marks your generation, and its house is where you most want freedom and where life is most likely to surprise you.
## Uranus by generation (approximate years)
* Aries (about 1927 to 1935 and 2010 to 2018): Pioneers and disruptors. A bold, independent and impatient generation.
* Taurus (about 1935 to 1942 and 2018 to 2026): Change in money, land and values. A generation that rethinks security.
* Gemini (about 1942 to 1948 and from 2026): Change through ideas and communication. A curious, restless generation.
* Cancer (about 1948 to 1955): Change in home, family and belonging.
* Leo (about 1955 to 1962): Change through creative self expression and individuality.
* Virgo (about 1962 to 1969): Change in work, health and daily life.
* Libra (about 1968 to 1975): Change in relationships and in ideas of fairness.
* Scorpio (about 1975 to 1981): Change in intimacy, power and what is hidden.
* Sagittarius (about 1981 to 1988): Change in belief, travel and freedom.
* Capricorn (about 1988 to 1995): Change in structures, work and authority.
* Aquarius (about 1995 to 2003): Change through technology, community and ideals.
* Pisces (about 2003 to 2011): Change through imagination, spirit and sensitivity.
## Uranus through the houses
* 1st house: You are original and unpredictable, and you may change your image suddenly.
* 2nd house: Unusual ways of earning and a changing relationship with money and values.
* 3rd house: An inventive, restless mind. Surprising words and ideas, and unusual siblings or surroundings.
* 4th house: An unusual or unsettled home life. Sudden moves, and you may feel like the odd one out in your family.
* 5th house: Unconventional romance and creativity, and sudden attractions.
* 6th house: You need freedom in work and an unusual routine, and may work with technology or alternatives.
* 7th house: You need freedom in partnership. Unusual or sudden relationships, and a need for space.
* 8th house: Sudden changes in intimacy and shared resources, and an interest in the occult and transformation.
* 9th house: You are drawn to unconventional beliefs, to travel and to radical ideas.
* 10th house: An unusual career. You may change direction suddenly and need freedom in your work.
* 11th house: A natural place for Uranus. You find your people among rebels, innovators and friends who are different.
* 12th house: Hidden sparks and sudden inner awakenings. Insight comes in solitude.
past: Uranus is read as the part of you that has always been the outsider, the rebel or the one who saw ahead. In past-life astrology he points to lives of breaking away, and to a restless memory of being shut in or of being ahead of your time.
## Stories it may point to

A strong Uranus may suggest lives as the revolutionary, the inventor, the exile or the lone thinker. The need for freedom can feel desperate, as if it were a question of survival. In some readings, sudden endings and abrupt leaving in the past leave a feeling that closeness is dangerous or that you must always be ready to go.
Uranus in the twelfth house is sometimes read as a soul that held its originality in secret, and is only now bringing it into the open.
## The lesson
To be free without being alone, and to bring your originality into the world in a way that others can receive.
## Questions to sit with
* Where do I feel I do not belong, and is that a choice or a wound?
* What would I change if I could?
* How can I be free and stay connected?
hidden: Uranus rules the unusual, and in astrology he is the planet of astrology itself, of lightning flashes of insight and of the alternative. A strong Uranus is often drawn to the occult precisely because it is outside the ordinary.
## In practice

People with a prominent Uranus often find that intuition arrives suddenly, in flashes or odd synchronicities. They may be drawn to the newest and most unconventional forms of practice, to technology and astrology, and to groups of like minded people who share an interest.

items.name: Neptune
items.summary: Dreams, intuition and the dissolving of boundaries.
basics: Neptune is the planet of imagination, compassion and spirit. It also stands for illusion, confusion and escape. It rules Pisces, and it was discovered in 1846. It takes about fourteen years to move through a sign and about a hundred and sixty five years to circle the zodiac, so its sign marks a long generation and its house is the personal part.

Neptune is the part of you that senses something more. It is music, dreams, longing, faith and the feeling of being part of everything. It dissolves boundaries, which can be beautiful and also bewildering.
## What it governs
Dreams, intuition, imagination, compassion, spirituality, art, music, illusion, idealism, addiction, confusion and sacrifice.
## At its best
A well used Neptune is compassionate, creative and spiritually sensitive. You can feel what others feel, you find beauty in the unseen and you can bring a vision into the world.
## When it is hard
Neptune can bring confusion, over idealising, escapism, being easily deceived or losing yourself in other people. It needs grounding, honesty and good boundaries.
## Finding it in your chart
The glyph is a trident. Its sign marks your generation, and its house is where you long for something more and where things feel blurred or magical.
## Neptune by generation (approximate years)
* Virgo (about 1929 to 1943): A generation shaped by war and hardship. Idealism turned into service and duty.
* Libra (about 1943 to 1957): A generation of ideals about peace, love and partnership.
* Scorpio (about 1957 to 1970): A generation of deep, hidden currents, secrets and transformation of ideals.
* Sagittarius (about 1970 to 1984): A generation seeking spiritual meaning and freedom of belief.
* Capricorn (about 1984 to 1998): A generation dissolving and rebuilding old structures.
* Aquarius (about 1998 to 2012): A generation of digital, collective and borderless ideals.
* Pisces (about 2012 to 2026): A generation in its own sign, deeply sensitive and imaginative.
* Aries (about 2026 to 2039): A coming generation of spiritual pioneers.
* Earlier signs (Leo and before): Generations born before about 1929, now very few.
## Neptune through the houses
* 1st house: A dreamy, impressionable presence. You may feel you are not quite sure who you are, and others project onto you.
* 2nd house: Fluid with money and values. You may give generously and need to guard against confusion over finances.
* 3rd house: An imaginative, intuitive mind. You may find precise words hard, and be a poet or storyteller.
* 4th house: A home that is a sanctuary, and a family with some mystery or confusion.
* 5th house: Romantic, artistic and idealistic. You may fall in love with the idea of someone.
* 6th house: You are sensitive in work and health and need a healthy routine. You may be drawn to healing work.
* 7th house: You idealise partners and need to see them clearly. Spiritual connections.
* 8th house: Mystical and psychic depth. Intuitive about hidden things and drawn to the occult.
* 9th house: You seek spiritual meaning and are drawn to mystical beliefs, long journeys and the ocean.
* 10th house: A vague or inspired career path. You may work in the arts, healing or spiritual fields.
* 11th house: You are idealistic in friendships and groups, and can be drawn to causes, or disillusioned by them.
* 12th house: A natural place for Neptune. Deep intuition, vivid dreams and a rich, hidden spiritual life.
past: Neptune is read as a faint memory of the sacred. In past-life astrology it points to lives of devotion, sacrifice, art or mysticism, and to the longing that remains: for a time, a place or a feeling that you cannot quite name.
## Stories it may point to

A strong Neptune is often linked with lives as a monk, nun, mystic, healer, artist or the one who gave everything for others. It can also suggest lives of illusion, in which you were deceived, or escaped into dreams, drink or sleep. Strong pulls to water, to music or to a past time are commonly described.
A person with a prominent Neptune may carry an old habit of rescuing others or sacrificing themselves, and an equally old wish to dissolve and be at peace.
## The lesson
To keep your sensitivity and your boundaries together: to be compassionate without being swallowed, and to bring your dreams into the world without losing yourself.
## Questions to sit with
* What do I long for that I cannot name?
* Where do I rescue others, or escape from myself?
* How can I stay grounded and still listen to the unseen?
hidden: Neptune rules the psychic and the mystical. In the hidden chart it is linked with dreams, visions, mediumship, tarot, the sense of the veil being thin and the pull to merge with something greater.
## In practice

People with a prominent Neptune often have vivid dreams, strong intuition and an ease with symbolic and visionary practices. Because Neptune blurs edges, it works best with grounding: eating well, sleeping, keeping routines and cleansing practices after intense work. It rewards honesty about what is intuition and what is wishing.

items.name: Pluto
basics: Pluto is the planet of transformation. It shows where you meet deep change, power and the things that are hidden. It rules Scorpio, and it was discovered in 1930. Its orbit is uneven: it takes between twelve and thirty one years to move through a sign, and about two hundred and forty eight years to circle the zodiac. Its sign marks a long generation, and its house is where it is most personal.
Pluto breaks down what is no longer true and rebuilds from the roots. It is slow, deep and often uncomfortable, and what it leaves behind tends to be stronger than what it took.
## What it governs
Transformation, power, control, obsession, death and rebirth, secrets, the unconscious, healing, survival and the underworld.
## At its best
A well used Pluto is powerful, honest and deeply resilient. You can face what others avoid, you can heal and transform, and you can help others through hard times.
## When it is hard
Pluto can bring control issues, jealousy, obsession, power struggles, or a feeling of being at the mercy of forces beyond you. The work is to face the shadow and to use power responsibly.
## Finding it in your chart

The glyph is a circle and a crescent above a cross, or sometimes the letters P and L. Its sign marks your generation, and its house is where you are transformed and where you meet the greatest intensity.
## Pluto by generation (approximate years)
* Cancer (about 1914 to 1939): A generation shaped by war and loss, with deep ties to family and security.
* Leo (about 1938 to 1958): The generation of rebuilding, and of new ideas about the self and creativity.
* Virgo (about 1956 to 1972): A generation transforming work, health and service.
* Libra (about 1971 to 1984): A generation transforming relationships and ideas of fairness.
* Scorpio (about 1983 to 1995): A generation facing power, sexuality, secrets and the shadow.
* Sagittarius (about 1995 to 2008): A generation transforming belief, information and the global view.
* Capricorn (about 2008 to 2024): A generation growing up as old structures and institutions are rebuilt.
* Aquarius (about 2024 to 2044): A coming generation transforming technology, community and collective power.
* Earlier signs (Gemini and before): Generations born before about 1914, now very few.
## Pluto through the houses
* 1st house: A powerful, intense presence. You may reinvent yourself more than once.
* 2nd house: Intense about money and values. You may lose and rebuild resources, and learn your true worth.
* 3rd house: A penetrating mind. You may speak with great power, and face lessons about secrets and honesty.
* 4th house: Deep family intensity and transformation, and powerful ancestral patterns.
* 5th house: Intense in love, creativity and play, and powerful attractions.
* 6th house: You transform through work and health. You may become a healer or an expert in your field.
* 7th house: Intense, transformative relationships and power dynamics, which teach you about control and trust.
* 8th house: A natural place for Pluto. Deep intimacy, the occult, death and rebirth, and great psychological power.
* 9th house: Transformation of belief. You are drawn to the deep and the taboo in philosophy and religion.
* 10th house: A powerful public role. You may rise, fall and rebuild in your career and reputation.
* 11th house: Intense friendships and groups. You may transform through community, or hold power in it.
* 12th house: Deep unconscious material and hidden power. Transformation is private and happens in solitude.
past: Pluto is read as the deepest layer of the past. In past-life astrology he points to lives of power or powerlessness, loss, survival and rebirth, and to the intense patterns that still ask to be healed.
## Stories it may point to

A strong Pluto is often linked with lives of great power, such as rulers or priests, or great suffering, such as persecution or war. Many people read an intense fear of loss, of being controlled, or of one's own power as a Plutonic memory. Obsessions, a fascination with death or the dark, and a powerful intuition for what is hidden in people are also commonly described.
The sign of Pluto marks the generation's shared story. The house shows where your personal one is working itself out.
## Pluto through the houses, as a past-life theme
* 1st house: An old identity of power, or of having it taken from you. The work is to own your strength without dominating or hiding.
* 2nd house: Old experiences of loss or of controlling resources. The work is to trust your worth.
* 3rd house: Old secrets, censorship or the power of words. The work is to speak truthfully.
* 4th house: Old family power and trauma. The work is to heal what you inherited and to build a safe home.
* 5th house: Old intense loves and losses. The work is to love without control.
* 6th house: Old lives of service, labour or healing. The work is to use your skill for health, and to rest.
* 7th house: Old power struggles in partnership. The work is to meet as equals.
* 8th house: The deepest layer. Old experiences of death, betrayal and intense bonds. The work is to trust, and to be transformed.
* 9th house: Old dogma or persecution for belief. The work is to find your own truth.
* 10th house: Old public power or humiliation. The work is to claim your calling with integrity.
* 11th house: Old group intensity, such as secret societies or being cast out. The work is to find healthy community.
* 12th house: Hidden power, exile or retreat. The work is to bring your depth into the light.
## The lesson
To face what is hidden in you, to let the old die and to use your power with care. Pluto gives you great strength once you have been through it.
## Questions to sit with
* Where do I fear losing control?
* What has ended in my life that I am still holding on to?
* What power do I have that I have been afraid to use?
hidden: Pluto rules the underworld, secrets and transformation. In the hidden chart he is the planet of shadow work and of the deepest forms of change: the descent, the sacrifice and the return. He is linked with death and rebirth themes, psychology and the occult, and with a pull towards what lies beneath the surface.
## In practice

People with a prominent Pluto are often drawn to the shadow side of practice: inner work, ancestor and underworld themes, death meditation, and rituals of ending and renewal. This is serious work, and it is best done at a pace you can manage, with support when it brings up difficult material.

groups.name: Signs
groups.blurb: The twelve signs and their style.

items.name: Aries
basics: Aries is the first sign of the zodiac. It is a cardinal fire sign, symbolised by the ram and ruled by Mars. The Sun is in Aries from about March 21 to April 19. It opens the zodiacal year at the spring equinox, so it is the sign of new beginnings.
## Keywords
Courage, initiative, independence, honesty, energy, competition, impatience, pioneering and a love of a challenge.
## At its best
Aries is brave, honest and full of energy. It is the one who goes first, stands up for others and is not afraid of a fresh start. It brings warmth and enthusiasm, and it recovers quickly.
## When it is hard
Aries can be impatient, impulsive, quick tempered or selfish, and it can find it hard to finish things. It can start a fight before it has thought, and it may find patience and listening difficult.
## In love
Direct and passionate. Aries loves the chase and the spark, and needs a partner who can meet its energy and does not mind its independence. It forgives quickly and does not hold grudges.
## At work
A natural leader and starter. It does well in roles with independence, action and a challenge, such as sport, business, emergency work and anything pioneering.
## Finding it in your chart

Your Sun, Moon and Rising signs are the three most visible places for Aries, but every planet is in a sign, and each one takes on its flavour. Any planet in Aries will lean towards the qualities above, in the way that planet works. A sign is a style, and not a fixed fate.
past: In past-life astrology Aries is the sign of the warrior, the pioneer and the one who stood alone. It is often read as a soul that has fought for survival and for its own place, and that still carries the instinct to go first and to be ready for a fight.
## Stories it may point to

People with a strong Aries theme sometimes describe a feeling of always having to defend themselves, of being the first to arrive or to leave, or of an old, physical readiness to act in danger. It can also point to lives of being held back, with the energy that did not get used now pushing for expression.
## The lesson
To use your courage on behalf of what you love, and to learn that you do not have to fight alone. The work is patience, listening, and trusting that others will come with you.
## Questions to sit with
* Where do I feel I have to fight?
* What would I begin if I were not afraid of failing?
* Who can I let help me?

items.name: Taurus
items.summary: Steadiness, the senses and what you value.
basics: Taurus is the second sign of the zodiac. It is a fixed earth sign, symbolised by the bull and ruled by Venus. The Sun is in Taurus from about April 20 to May 20. It is the sign of the spring season at its fullest, when the earth is growing, and it is the zodiac's sign of the senses and of the land.
## Keywords
Patience, loyalty, stability, sensuality, comfort, determination, stubbornness, beauty, material security and a love of the good things.
## At its best
Taurus is steady, loyal and wonderfully grounded. It brings calm, builds things that last and has a gift for enjoying life: good food, beautiful objects, nature and touch.
## When it is hard
Taurus can be stubborn, possessive and resistant to change. It may cling to comfort and money, and once it has made up its mind it is very hard to move. Anger comes slowly, but it can be immovable.
## In love
Loyal, sensual and slow to commit but steady once it does. Taurus shows love through time, touch, food and reliability, and values comfort and trust.
## At work
Patient and reliable. It does well where there is craft, beauty, nature or finance, and it builds towards security over time. Good in roles that value steadiness.
## Finding it in your chart

Your Sun, Moon and Rising signs are the three most visible places for Taurus, but every planet is in a sign, and each one takes on its flavour. Any planet in Taurus will lean towards the qualities above, in the way that planet works. A sign is a style, and not a fixed fate.
past: In past-life astrology, Taurus points to lives close to the land, craft, wealth or hunger. It is often read as a soul that has known great comfort, or great lack, and that now holds on tightly to safety and possessions.
## Stories it may point to

People with a strong Taurus theme sometimes describe an instant, deep calm in nature, an old love of a particular craft or a very strong reaction to money and food. It can also carry an old fear of poverty, or an old sense of owning too much and being owned by it.
## The lesson
To find security within and not only in what you own, and to know what you truly value. The work is flexibility, and trusting that you will be provided for.
## Questions to sit with
* What do I cling to for safety?
* What do I value that has nothing to do with money?
* Where am I stubborn, and what am I afraid of if I move?

items.name: Gemini
basics: Gemini is the third sign of the zodiac. It is a mutable air sign, symbolised by the twins and ruled by Mercury. The Sun is in Gemini from about May 21 to June 20. It is the sign of the mind and of communication, and it likes to know a little about everything.
## Keywords
Curiosity, wit, communication, adaptability, learning, versatility, restlessness, humour and a love of variety.
## At its best
Gemini is quick, curious and charming. It makes connections between people and ideas, learns fast and keeps things light. It is a natural storyteller and an excellent friend to talk to.
## When it is hard
Gemini can be scattered, nervous or inconsistent. It can say what people want to hear, avoid depth and get bored easily. It may find it hard to rest or to sit with feeling.
## In love
Playful, talkative and flirtatious. Gemini needs mental connection first, and a partner who keeps it curious. It can find commitment hard if it feels bored or boxed in.
## At work
A natural communicator. It does well in writing, teaching, media, sales, languages and anything that involves variety, information and people.
## Finding it in your chart

Your Sun, Moon and Rising signs are the three most visible places for Gemini, but every planet is in a sign, and each one takes on its flavour. Any planet in Gemini will lean towards the qualities above, in the way that planet works. A sign is a style, and not a fixed fate.
past: In past-life astrology, Gemini points to lives as the messenger, trader, writer or teacher. It is often read as a soul that has lived among many voices, travelled between places and gathered stories.
## Stories it may point to

People with a strong Gemini theme sometimes describe a gift for languages, an old sense of being at home on the road, or a feeling of having had two lives at once. It can also suggest lives in which words were dangerous, and what was said had a cost.
## The lesson
To bring depth to your curiosity, and to use words with care. The work is focus, and listening as much as you speak.
## Questions to sit with
* What have I always loved to learn?
* Where do I stay on the surface?
* What do I most want to say?

items.name: Cancer
basics: Cancer is the fourth sign of the zodiac. It is a cardinal water sign, symbolised by the crab and ruled by the Moon. The Sun is in Cancer from about June 21 to July 22. It begins at the summer solstice, and it is the sign of home, family and emotional memory.
## Keywords
Nurture, sensitivity, protection, memory, intuition, home, family, moodiness, loyalty and emotional depth.
## At its best
Cancer is tender, intuitive and deeply caring. It makes a home wherever it goes, remembers what matters and protects the people it loves. Its sensitivity is a gift for noticing what others need.
## When it is hard
Cancer can be moody, clingy, defensive or hold on to the past. Like the crab, it can retreat into its shell when hurt, and it may find it hard to let go of people or of resentment.
## In love
Devoted, protective and emotionally deep. Cancer needs to feel safe and loved, and shows love through care, food and a home. It takes time to trust, and once it does it is loyal.
## At work
It does well in care, hospitality, teaching, healing, family business and anything that involves nurture. It often works best in a warm, supportive environment.
## Finding it in your chart

Your Sun, Moon and Rising signs are the three most visible places for Cancer, but every planet is in a sign, and each one takes on its flavour. Any planet in Cancer will lean towards the qualities above, in the way that planet works. A sign is a style, and not a fixed fate.
past: In past-life astrology, Cancer points to lives of mothering, caring and belonging, and also to lives of loss of home. It is often read as a soul with a strong sense of family across lifetimes.
## Stories it may point to

People with a strong Cancer theme sometimes describe a very old tie to a particular place, a longing for a home they cannot name, or an intense protectiveness of children and the vulnerable. It can also point to old losses: of a mother, a child, or a home, and a wariness of leaving.
## The lesson
To build a feeling of home inside yourself, and to care for others without losing yourself. The work is letting go, and trusting that love does not end when it changes.
## Questions to sit with
* What does home mean to me?
* Who am I still holding on to?
* How can I care for myself as well as I care for others?

items.name: Leo
basics: Leo is the fifth sign of the zodiac. It is a fixed fire sign, symbolised by the lion and ruled by the Sun. The Sun is in Leo from about July 23 to August 22. It is the sign of the heart, of creativity and of the joy of being alive, and it is the only sign ruled by the Sun.
## Keywords
Warmth, generosity, creativity, pride, loyalty, drama, leadership, confidence and a need to be appreciated.
## At its best
Leo is warm, generous and full of heart. It lights up a room, loves openly and makes others feel special. It is creative, loyal and brave, and it is happy to take the lead.
## When it is hard

Leo can be proud, stubborn or attention seeking. It can be hurt very deeply by being ignored or criticised, and may find it hard to admit that it is wrong. Beneath the pride is often a need for reassurance.
## In love
Romantic, loyal and generous. Leo loves to love and to be adored, and needs a partner who gives warmth and praise. It is playful and protective.
## At work
A natural performer and leader. It does well in creative work, performance, leadership, teaching, entertainment and anything that gives it a stage.
## Finding it in your chart

Your Sun, Moon and Rising signs are the three most visible places for Leo, but every planet is in a sign, and each one takes on its flavour. Any planet in Leo will lean towards the qualities above, in the way that planet works. A sign is a style, and not a fixed fate.
past: In past-life astrology, Leo is the sign of the leader, the performer and the royal, and also of being overlooked. It is often read as a soul that has known the light of the stage, and the pain of losing it.
## Stories it may point to

People with a strong Leo theme sometimes describe a feeling of belonging on a stage, an old memory of being admired or of falling from grace, or a strong need to be recognised. It can also point to lives of being unseen, with the heart still waiting to be expressed.
## The lesson
To let your heart be seen without needing applause, and to shine for the joy of it. The work is generosity, and sharing the light.
## Questions to sit with
* When do I feel truly seen?
* What do I create for the love of it?
* How can I give without needing a reward?

items.name: Virgo
