basics: Virgo is the sixth sign of the zodiac. It is a mutable earth sign, symbolised by the maiden and ruled by Mercury. The Sun is in Virgo from about August 23 to September 22. It is the sign of the harvest, of work and of skill, and it notices what needs to be made better.
## Keywords
Service, analysis, skill, health, precision, modesty, perfectionism, craft and practical care.
## At its best
Virgo is thoughtful, capable and kind. It notices the details others miss and quietly makes things work. It is a gifted helper, healer and craftsperson, with a modest and genuine wish to be of use.
## When it is hard
Virgo can be critical, anxious or hard on itself. It can worry about the small things and hold itself to impossible standards. It may find it hard to relax, or to accept praise.
## In love
Devoted, thoughtful and shy at first. Virgo shows love through practical acts and attention to detail, and needs a partner who values its care.
## At work
Excellent in any field that needs skill and detail: health, research, editing, crafts, administration and service. It often works quietly and well.
## Finding it in your chart

Your Sun, Moon and Rising signs are the three most visible places for Virgo, but every planet is in a sign, and each one takes on its flavour. Any planet in Virgo will lean towards the qualities above, in the way that planet works. A sign is a style, and not a fixed fate.
past: In past-life astrology, Virgo points to lives of service: healers, craftspeople, herbalists, scribes and servants. It is often read as a soul that learned its skill through years of patient work, and that gave much of itself to others.
## Stories it may point to

People with a strong Virgo theme sometimes describe a natural feel for herbs or healing, an old habit of perfectionism, or a feeling of having been useful but unseen. It can also carry a sense that you must earn your place by working.
## The lesson
To value yourself beyond your usefulness, and to accept that you are enough as you are. The work is self compassion, and trusting that things do not have to be perfect.
## Questions to sit with
* Where do I feel I must earn my place?
* What is my natural skill?
* How can I be as kind to myself as I am to others?
hidden: Virgo is the sign of herbs, remedies and careful craft. In the hidden chart it is linked with practical magic and the healing arts, and with the discipline of working a ritual or a recipe exactly.
## In practice

People with a strong Virgo are often drawn to herbalism, cleansing, tidying as ritual, healing work and the careful detail of correspondences and timing. It is the witch who keeps the garden, labels every jar and knows which plant to use.

items.name: Libra
basics: Libra is the seventh sign of the zodiac. It is a cardinal air sign, symbolised by the scales and ruled by Venus. The Sun is in Libra from about September 23 to October 22. It begins at the autumn equinox, when day and night are equal, and it is the sign of balance and of partnership.
## Keywords
Harmony, fairness, partnership, diplomacy, beauty, charm, indecision, justice and a love of peace.
## At its best
Libra is gracious, fair and gifted with people. It sees both sides, softens conflict and brings beauty and balance. It is a skilled diplomat, a loyal partner and a lover of art and harmony.
## When it is hard
Libra can be indecisive, people pleasing or avoid conflict at all costs. It may lose itself in others, or put on a pleasant surface while feeling quite different underneath.
## In love
Romantic, charming and committed to partnership. Libra loves being in a pair and seeks fairness and beauty in love. It may find it hard to be alone.
## At work
It does well in law, diplomacy, design, the arts, counselling and any role involving collaboration, fairness or beauty.
## Finding it in your chart

Your Sun, Moon and Rising signs are the three most visible places for Libra, but every planet is in a sign, and each one takes on its flavour. Any planet in Libra will lean towards the qualities above, in the way that planet works. A sign is a style, and not a fixed fate.
past: In past-life astrology, Libra points to lives defined by partnership, law and diplomacy. It is often read as a soul that has built its identity through relationships, and has been shaped by marriage, alliance and negotiation.
## Stories it may point to

People with a strong Libra theme sometimes describe an old sense of a soul partner, a love of courtrooms or ceremony, or a habit of keeping the peace at their own cost. It can also suggest lives in which fairness was denied, and the wish for justice is now deep.
## The lesson
To choose for yourself while staying in relationship, and to understand that peace is not the absence of conflict. The work is decision, and speaking your truth.
## Questions to sit with
* Where do I give up my own needs to keep the peace?
* What do I really want, and what do I tell myself I should want?
* What would fairness look like in my life?

items.name: Scorpio
basics: Scorpio is the eighth sign of the zodiac. It is a fixed water sign, symbolised by the scorpion and ruled by Pluto (and Mars in the traditional system). The Sun is in Scorpio from about October 23 to November 21. It is the sign of depth, of secrets and of transformation, and it does not look away from what is hard.
## Keywords
Intensity, passion, loyalty, power, secrecy, transformation, psychology, resilience and a drive to the truth.
## At its best
Scorpio is powerful, perceptive and deeply loyal. It sees beneath the surface, faces what others avoid and has an extraordinary capacity for transformation. It is passionate, resilient and honest.
## When it is hard
Scorpio can be controlling, jealous, secretive or hold grudges. It may test people, find it hard to trust or retreat into silence. Its intensity can overwhelm both itself and others.
## In love
All or nothing. Scorpio loves deeply and seeks real intimacy, and it needs trust and honesty. It is fiercely loyal, and it does not forgive betrayal easily.
## At work
It does well in research, psychology, medicine, investigation, finance, crisis work and anything that goes deep. It brings focus and persistence.
## Finding it in your chart

Your Sun, Moon and Rising signs are the three most visible places for Scorpio, but every planet is in a sign, and each one takes on its flavour. Any planet in Scorpio will lean towards the qualities above, in the way that planet works. A sign is a style, and not a fixed fate.
past: In past-life astrology, Scorpio points to lives touched by power, betrayal, secrets and death. It is often read as a soul that has been through the depths, and has come back with great resilience and a wariness of trust.
## Stories it may point to

People with a strong Scorpio theme sometimes describe a deep familiarity with death or loss, an intense fear of betrayal, or a feeling of having survived something enormous. It can also suggest lives in which you held power over others, and the lesson now is to use it with care.
## The lesson
To trust again, to let go of control and to allow yourself to be seen. The work is forgiveness, and learning that vulnerability is not weakness.
## Questions to sit with
* What have I survived that I rarely speak about?
* Where do I hold on to control?
* Who could I trust a little more?
hidden: Scorpio is the classic occult sign, drawn to mystery, the taboo and the unseen. In the hidden chart it is linked with shadow work, the study of death and rebirth, and the pull towards what is hidden.
## In practice

People with a strong Scorpio are often drawn to the depths of practice: shadow work, the study of death and the underworld, tarot, ritual of transformation and the psychology of the unconscious. Scorpio is also the sign of discretion, and many keep their practice private.

items.name: Sagittarius
basics: Sagittarius is the ninth sign of the zodiac. It is a mutable fire sign, symbolised by the archer and ruled by Jupiter. The Sun is in Sagittarius from about November 22 to December 21. It is the sign of the seeker, the traveller and the philosopher, and it always aims at something further away.
## Keywords
Freedom, adventure, honesty, optimism, learning, travel, philosophy, humour and a love of the big picture.
## At its best
Sagittarius is optimistic, honest and adventurous. It brings humour, faith and a sense of possibility. It loves to explore, to learn and to share what it has found, and it makes others feel hopeful.
## When it is hard
Sagittarius can be tactless, restless or careless with promises. It may preach, overreach or avoid commitment in the name of freedom. It can find the details and the feelings of everyday life hard.
## In love
Free spirited, warm and honest. Sagittarius needs a partner who is also a friend, and who gives it room to roam. It loves adventure and laughter.
## At work
It does well in teaching, travel, publishing, philosophy, law, outdoor work and anything with a wider horizon.
## Finding it in your chart

Your Sun, Moon and Rising signs are the three most visible places for Sagittarius, but every planet is in a sign, and each one takes on its flavour. Any planet in Sagittarius will lean towards the qualities above, in the way that planet works. A sign is a style, and not a fixed fate.
past: In past-life astrology, Sagittarius suggests lives of travel, teaching, faith and pilgrimage. It is often read as a soul that has wandered widely, and carries a deep sense of purpose and belief.
## Stories it may point to

People with a strong Sagittarius theme sometimes describe an old restlessness, a pull to far away places or a deep faith that is hard to explain. It can also point to lives of dogma or preaching, and the lesson now is humility and openness.
## The lesson
To find meaning in the here and now, and to hold your truths lightly. The work is commitment, and listening to others' truths.
## Questions to sit with
* What do I believe, and where did it come from?
* Where do I run when things get close?
* What is my next real adventure?

items.name: Capricorn
basics: Capricorn is the tenth sign of the zodiac. It is a cardinal earth sign, symbolised by the sea-goat and ruled by Saturn. The Sun is in Capricorn from about December 22 to January 19. It begins at the winter solstice, and it is the sign of discipline, of time and of the climb towards a goal.
## Keywords
Ambition, discipline, responsibility, patience, practicality, authority, reserve, endurance and a respect for tradition.
## At its best
Capricorn is capable, patient and reliable. It builds slowly and well, takes responsibility and keeps its word. It often grows more relaxed and wise with age, as it earns what it sets out to achieve.
## When it is hard
Capricorn can be stern, cold, pessimistic or overly focused on status. It may carry too much responsibility alone, hold back its feelings and find rest and play difficult.
## In love
Reserved and committed. Capricorn takes love seriously, shows it through reliability and practical care, and warms with time.
## At work
It does well in management, finance, law, engineering, government and any field with structure, authority and long term goals.
## Finding it in your chart

Your Sun, Moon and Rising signs are the three most visible places for Capricorn, but every planet is in a sign, and each one takes on its flavour. Any planet in Capricorn will lean towards the qualities above, in the way that planet works. A sign is a style, and not a fixed fate.
past: In past-life astrology, Capricorn points to lives of duty, rank, hard work and heavy responsibility. It is often read as a soul that has carried a great deal, and learned to be strong because there was no one else.
## Stories it may point to

People with a strong Capricorn theme sometimes describe an old sense of being an adult from childhood, a fear of failure or poverty, or the feeling of having to earn the right to rest. It can also point to lives of authority, and the weight that came with it.
## The lesson
To lighten the load, to accept support and to remember that you are worth more than what you achieve. The work is rest, and letting yourself be cared for.
## Questions to sit with
* What responsibility do I carry that is not mine to carry?
* What would I do if I did not have to prove anything?
* Who can I ask for help?

items.name: Aquarius
basics: Aquarius is the eleventh sign of the zodiac. It is a fixed air sign, symbolised by the water-bearer and ruled by Uranus (and Saturn in the traditional system). The Sun is in Aquarius from about January 20 to February 18. It is the sign of the future, of the group and of the original idea, and it looks at the world from a little distance.
## Keywords
Originality, independence, community, ideals, innovation, detachment, humanitarianism and eccentricity.
## At its best
Aquarius is original, humane and forward thinking. It brings fresh ideas, loves people as a whole and stands up for what it believes. It is a loyal friend and a gifted innovator.
## When it is hard
Aquarius can be aloof, stubborn or rebellious for its own sake. It may find it hard to share personal feeling, and can seem cool or disconnected, though it cares very much.
## In love
Friendship first. Aquarius needs freedom, mental connection and a partner who is also a friend. It loves unconventional ways of relating, and values honesty.
## At work
It does well in technology, science, activism, community work, the arts and anywhere that values originality and ideals.
## Finding it in your chart

Your Sun, Moon and Rising signs are the three most visible places for Aquarius, but every planet is in a sign, and each one takes on its flavour. Any planet in Aquarius will lean towards the qualities above, in the way that planet works. A sign is a style, and not a fixed fate.
past: In past-life astrology, Aquarius suggests lives as the outsider, the reformer or the visionary. It is often read as a soul that has stood apart, ahead of its time or alone for the sake of an idea.
## Stories it may point to

People with a strong Aquarius theme sometimes describe a lifelong sense of being from somewhere else, an old interest in brotherhoods and circles, or a restless memory of being shut out. It can also suggest lives of great community, and the ache of losing it.
## The lesson
To bring your originality into the group, and to let people close. The work is the heart, and being personally seen and not only admired for your ideas.
## Questions to sit with
* Where do I feel I do not belong?
* What ideal would I give my life to?
* Who have I kept at a distance?
hidden: Aquarius rules the unusual and the future. In the hidden chart it is linked with astrology itself, with new ideas and the alternative, and with groups that gather around a shared interest.
## In practice

People with a strong Aquarius are often drawn to astrology, to modern and experimental forms of practice, and to online and offline circles of like minded people. It is the sign of the study group, the coven that meets for a shared purpose and the one who invents a new way of doing an old thing.

items.name: Pisces
basics: Pisces is the twelfth sign of the zodiac. It is a mutable water sign, symbolised by the fishes and ruled by Neptune (and Jupiter in the traditional system). The Sun is in Pisces from about February 19 to March 20. It is the last sign of the zodiac, and it holds something of all the others. It is the sign of dreams, compassion and the unseen.
## Keywords
Compassion, imagination, intuition, sensitivity, creativity, spirituality, devotion, escapism and empathy.
## At its best
Pisces is gentle, intuitive and deeply creative. It feels what others feel, sees beauty in the unseen and has a spiritual or artistic depth. It forgives easily and gives generously.
## When it is hard
Pisces can be vague, escapist or easily overwhelmed. It may absorb other people's feelings, avoid difficult truths, or be drawn to rescuing or being rescued. Boundaries are its great lesson.
## In love
Romantic, devoted and selfless. Pisces loves unconditionally, and seeks a soul connection. It needs a partner who is kind, and who helps it stay grounded.
## At work
It does well in the arts, music, healing, counselling, spirituality, charity and anywhere that uses imagination and compassion.
## Finding it in your chart

Your Sun, Moon and Rising signs are the three most visible places for Pisces, but every planet is in a sign, and each one takes on its flavour. Any planet in Pisces will lean towards the qualities above, in the way that planet works. A sign is a style, and not a fixed fate.
past: In past-life astrology, Pisces points to lives of the mystic, the artist and the healer, and also of sacrifice and escape. It is often read as a soul with a very old tenderness, which has felt too much and sometimes tried to dissolve.
## Stories it may point to

People with a strong Pisces theme sometimes describe vivid dreams of other lives, a deep pull to water or the sacred, or an old habit of giving everything away. It can also point to lives of confinement or exile, and a longing to be free.
## The lesson
To keep your sensitivity and your boundaries together, and to bring your visions into the world. The work is grounding, and learning that compassion includes yourself.
## Questions to sit with
* Where do I give too much, or disappear?
* What do my dreams keep showing me?
* How can I stay grounded and still listen to the unseen?
hidden: Pisces is the sign of the veil. In the hidden chart it is linked with dreams, intuition, mediumship and the mystical, and with the need to protect your energy while you listen.
## In practice

People with a strong Pisces are often drawn to dreamwork, divination, music, water rituals and meditation. Because Pisces absorbs so much, cleansing, boundaries and time alone matter as much as the practice itself.

items.name: The First House
basics: The first house is an angular house, one of the four corners of the chart, so planets here are strong and visible. It is linked with Aries and Mars, which is its natural sign and ruler. It begins at the Ascendant, or Rising sign, which is the sign that was rising on the eastern horizon at the moment you were born. Different house systems divide the chart a little differently, but the Ascendant always marks the start of the first house.
## What it rules
Your body, appearance, first impressions, personality, instincts, the way you begin things and the way others see you before they know you.
## When it is strong
You are strongly yourself. Your presence is clear and others tend to notice you. You take the initiative and have a distinct style.
## When it is a challenge
You may feel exposed, or you may identify too much with how others see you. Learning where the mask ends and you begin is the work.
## Planets in this house
Planets here are very visible. They colour your appearance and your way of meeting the world, and they often show in how you move, speak and dress.
## The sign on this house

The sign on the edge of the house, called its cusp, colours how the area of life works for you, and the planet that rules that sign is called the house ruler. Follow it to the house it sits in to see how this area of life connects with the others. An empty house is not a weak one: it is simply read through its sign and its ruler.
past: The first house is read as the self you bring in with you and the role you step into on arrival. It is the face of this life, and often echoes an old way of being seen.
## Stories it may point to

Planets here sometimes point to a recognisable presence: you may remind people of someone, or feel you have worn this role before. A hidden or hard first house can suggest lives in which you could not be yourself openly.
## The lesson
To be yourself fully, and to know that you are allowed to take up space. The work is authenticity.
## Questions to sit with
* How do people see me when I walk into a room?
* Which part of me do I hide?
* Who would I be if I did not need to please?

items.name: The Second House
items.summary: Money, possessions and what you value.
basics: The second house is a succedent house, which follows an angular house and is about stabilising and building. It is linked with Taurus and Venus, which is its natural sign and ruler. It follows the Ascendant and is about what you build with the self you have begun.
## What it rules
Money, income, possessions, talents, values, self worth and your sense of what is secure.
## When it is strong
You have a good sense of value and know how to earn. Your skills are an asset, and you feel secure in what you own.
## When it is a challenge
Money and worth may feel linked in an anxious way. You may spend to feel better, hold on too tightly, or doubt that you deserve what you have.
## Planets in this house
Planets here show how you earn, what you value and how you feel about money. They often point to your natural talents.
## The sign on this house

The sign on the edge of the house, called its cusp, colours how the area of life works for you, and the planet that rules that sign is called the house ruler. Follow it to the house it sits in to see how this area of life connects with the others. An empty house is not a weak one: it is simply read through its sign and its ruler.
past: The second house points to old relationships with money and security: wealth, poverty, and the skills you earned. It shows where your sense of worth was built or damaged.
## Stories it may point to

People with planets here often describe a very strong reaction to money, either a fear of lack or an easy feeling of having enough. Talents that seem to come from nowhere are also linked with this house: a natural eye for craft, for beauty or for business.
## The lesson
To build your own security and to know that your worth does not depend on what you own. The work is trust.
## Questions to sit with
* What does security mean to me?
* What do I feel I am worth?
* Which of my talents do I take for granted?

items.name: The Third House
basics: The third house is a cadent house, which sits before an angular house and is about learning, adapting and preparing. It is linked with Gemini and Mercury, which is its natural sign and ruler. It is the house of the near and familiar, where the mind learns and connects.
## What it rules
Communication, learning, siblings, neighbours, short journeys, the everyday environment, speech, writing and early education.
## When it is strong
You are curious and communicative. You learn fast, make connections easily and keep in touch with the people around you.
## When it is a challenge
You may scatter your energy, talk too much or too little, or find the people close to you hard to understand. Early schooling may have been difficult.
## Planets in this house
Planets here show how you think and speak, and what your everyday world is like. They often point to a sibling or a neighbour who matters.
## The sign on this house

The sign on the edge of the house, called its cusp, colours how the area of life works for you, and the planet that rules that sign is called the house ruler. Follow it to the house it sits in to see how this area of life connects with the others. An empty house is not a weak one: it is simply read through its sign and its ruler.
past: The third house points to old bonds with those close to you and to skills of speech and writing. It can show who you were a sibling, a neighbour or a messenger to.
## Stories it may point to

People with planets here sometimes describe a gift for languages, a sense of knowing a place they have never visited or a very close tie with a brother or sister. A challenged third house can suggest old silence, censorship or a fear of speaking.
## The lesson
To speak with care and to trust that you will be heard. The work is voice.
## Questions to sit with
* Who have I always been close to?
* What do I find hard to say?
* What have I always been able to learn quickly?

items.name: The Fourth House
items.summary: Home, roots and the private self.
basics: The fourth house is an angular house, one of the four corners of the chart, so planets here are strong and visible. It is linked with Cancer and the Moon, which is its natural sign and ruler. It begins at the bottom of the chart, called the Imum Coeli or IC, and it is the base on which the whole chart stands.
## What it rules
Home, family, ancestry, childhood, the mother or one parent, the private self, land, property and your sense of belonging.
## When it is strong
You have a deep sense of roots and belonging. Home is a sanctuary and your family ties give you strength.
## When it is a challenge
Family may be complicated, or home may feel unsafe or unsettled. You may carry old family patterns or feel you do not belong anywhere.
## Planets in this house
Planets here describe your home and your family, and the part of you that is private and unseen. They are strongly linked with childhood and with who you are underneath.
## The sign on this house

The sign on the edge of the house, called its cusp, colours how the area of life works for you, and the planet that rules that sign is called the house ruler. Follow it to the house it sits in to see how this area of life connects with the others. An empty house is not a weak one: it is simply read through its sign and its ruler.
past: The fourth house is one of the strongest past-life houses. It is read as family lines, ancestral patterns and old homes. Planets here can suggest who you were close to and the place your soul calls home.
## Stories it may point to

People with planets here often describe a strong tie to ancestors, to a place or to a particular land. A feeling of coming home on first visiting somewhere, or of having a family from another time or country, is commonly mentioned. A challenged fourth house may suggest lost homes, exile or family conflict across generations.
## The lesson
To make a home inside yourself, and to heal what you have inherited. The work is belonging.
## Questions to sit with
* Where do I feel at home?
* Which family patterns do I repeat?
* What would I like to pass on, and what would I like to end?
hidden: The fourth house is linked with ancestors and with home magic: the hearth, family traditions and protecting a space. It is the house of the private altar and of the bones of the family.
## In practice

People with planets in the fourth house are often drawn to ancestor work, to family history, to hearth and kitchen magic and to making a home into a sacred space. Protection of the home, cleansing and keeping family rituals alive are all natural to this house.

items.name: The Fifth House
basics: The fifth house is a succedent house, which follows an angular house and is about stabilising and building. It is linked with Leo and the Sun, which is its natural sign and ruler. It is the house of joy: what you do for love and what you do for fun.
## What it rules
Creativity, romance, children, play, self expression, hobbies, risk taking and pleasure.
## When it is strong
You are expressive and playful. Creative work comes easily, romance is lively and you know how to enjoy life.
## When it is a challenge
Joy may feel blocked or guilty. You may be afraid to be seen, risk too much in love, or put your creativity aside for duty.
## Planets in this house
Planets here show how you create and play, how you love and what makes you feel alive. They often describe your relationship with children.
## The sign on this house

The sign on the edge of the house, called its cusp, colours how the area of life works for you, and the planet that rules that sign is called the house ruler. Follow it to the house it sits in to see how this area of life connects with the others. An empty house is not a weak one: it is simply read through its sign and its ruler.
past: The fifth house points to old artistry, love affairs and performance. It can show where you have already been a creator, and where joy was lost or taken away.
## Stories it may point to

People with planets here sometimes describe an old memory of the stage, of love affairs or of a child. A challenged fifth house may suggest old lives of duty with no room for play, or of love that was forbidden.
## The lesson
To allow joy and creativity back into your life, and to love without fear. The work is play.
## Questions to sit with
* What did I love to do as a child?
* What would I create if no one would see it?
* What does joy feel like in my body?

items.name: The Sixth House
basics: The sixth house is a cadent house, which sits before an angular house and is about learning, adapting and preparing. It is linked with Virgo and Mercury, which is its natural sign and ruler. It is the house of the everyday and the practical: what you do each day and how you look after yourself.
## What it rules
Daily work, routines, habits, skills, service, health habits, pets and the people you work for or with.
## When it is strong
You are conscientious and skilled. You find meaning in being useful, and you care well for your body and your environment.
## When it is a challenge
You may overwork, worry, feel ill at ease in jobs or neglect your own health. Learning to rest is often part of the work.
## Planets in this house
Planets here describe your working life and daily habits and how you care for your wellbeing. They often show the kind of service you are suited to.
## The sign on this house

The sign on the edge of the house, called its cusp, colours how the area of life works for you, and the planet that rules that sign is called the house ruler. Follow it to the house it sits in to see how this area of life connects with the others. An empty house is not a weak one: it is simply read through its sign and its ruler.
past: The sixth house points to lives of service, craft and duty. Planets here can show old devotion to work or to others, and a lesson about caring for yourself.
## Stories it may point to

People with planets here sometimes describe a natural skill with healing, herbs, crafts or care, an old feeling of having served in a household or workshop, or a deep need to be useful. A challenged sixth house may point to old drudgery, or to a feeling that you must work to deserve rest.
## The lesson
To serve without losing yourself, and to care for your own body as well as for others. The work is balance.
## Questions to sit with
* What work feels meaningful to me?
* Where do I overwork?
* How do I care for my own body?

items.name: The Seventh House
items.summary: Partnership and one to one relationships.
basics: The seventh house is an angular house, one of the four corners of the chart, so planets here are strong and visible. It is linked with Libra and Venus, which is its natural sign and ruler. It begins at the Descendant, directly opposite the Ascendant, and it is the house of the other.
## What it rules
Marriage, committed partnership, close friendships, business partners, open rivals and what you attract and project onto others.
## When it is strong
You are good at partnership and attract capable, balanced people. You grow through relationships and know how to cooperate.
## When it is a challenge
You may lose yourself in others, project your own qualities onto partners, or attract the same kind of person again and again. Conflict may arise in relationship.
## Planets in this house
Planets here describe the people you partner with and what you seek in them. They often show qualities you do not yet own in yourself.
## The sign on this house

The sign on the edge of the house, called its cusp, colours how the area of life works for you, and the planet that rules that sign is called the house ruler. Follow it to the house it sits in to see how this area of life connects with the others. An empty house is not a weak one: it is simply read through its sign and its ruler.
past: The seventh house is the house of soul partners. It is read as old bonds, the kind of person you keep meeting and the lessons exchanged in love. Planets here can suggest a familiar partner or an unfinished story.
## Stories it may point to

People with planets here often describe meeting someone and feeling they had always known them, or a pattern of repeating the same lessons in partnership. A challenged seventh house may point to old broken vows, power struggles or partnerships you could not choose.
## The lesson
To meet others as equals, and to own the qualities you look for in them. The work is relationship.
## Questions to sit with
* What kind of person do I keep attracting?
* What do I project onto my partners?
* What do I need to give myself?

items.name: The Eighth House
basics: The eighth house is a succedent house, which follows an angular house and is about stabilising and building. It is linked with Scorpio, Pluto and Mars, which is its natural sign and ruler. It is the house of what is shared and what is hidden, and of the deepest changes in a life.
## What it rules
Intimacy, sex, shared money, inheritance, debts, loss, death and rebirth, secrets, psychology and the occult.
## When it is strong
You are drawn to depth and have a talent for transformation. You are resilient, perceptive and unafraid of difficult subjects.
## When it is a challenge
You may fear loss or betrayal, struggle with control, or find it hard to trust or to share. Crisis may come again and again until a pattern is faced.
## Planets in this house
Planets here show where you are transformed and how you handle intimacy and shared resources. They are often linked with psychological depth.
## The sign on this house

The sign on the edge of the house, called its cusp, colours how the area of life works for you, and the planet that rules that sign is called the house ruler. Follow it to the house it sits in to see how this area of life connects with the others. An empty house is not a weak one: it is simply read through its sign and its ruler.
past: The eighth house is read as the house of past-life death and rebirth. It is linked with old loss, power, betrayal and survival. Planets here show where deep transformation is still being worked through.
## Stories it may point to

People with planets here often describe an unusual relationship with death, either fear or ease, a sense of having survived something enormous or a pull to the occult. A challenged eighth house may suggest old betrayals, losses of power or intense bonds that still hold you.
## The lesson
To trust, to share and to let go of what has ended. The work is surrender.
## Questions to sit with
* What have I lost that I am still grieving?
* Where do I hold on to control?
* What is ready to be transformed?
hidden: The eighth house is the classic occult house. It rules the mysteries, the unseen and the taboo, and it is linked with shadow work, death and rebirth themes, and the study of hidden knowledge.
## In practice

People with planets in the eighth house are often drawn to the depths of practice: shadow work, the study of death and the afterlife, tarot, psychology, sex magic as a subject of study and the work with the hidden self. This is serious ground, and it is best approached with care and good support.

items.name: The Ninth House
items.summary: Belief, travel and the search for meaning.
basics: The ninth house is a cadent house, which sits before an angular house and is about learning, adapting and preparing. It is linked with Sagittarius and Jupiter, which is its natural sign and ruler. It is the house of the wider view: what you believe and how you understand the world.
## What it rules
Higher learning, travel, foreign cultures, religion, philosophy, law, teaching, publishing and the search for meaning.
## When it is strong
You are curious about the world and love to learn, travel and teach. Your beliefs give you faith and direction.
## When it is a challenge
You may become dogmatic, restless or lose faith. You may struggle with what to believe, or feel you do not fit within a culture or tradition.
## Planets in this house
Planets here show how you search for meaning and what you believe. They often describe a calling to teach or to travel.
## The sign on this house

The sign on the edge of the house, called its cusp, colours how the area of life works for you, and the planet that rules that sign is called the house ruler. Follow it to the house it sits in to see how this area of life connects with the others. An empty house is not a weak one: it is simply read through its sign and its ruler.
past: The ninth house points to old teachers, travels and faiths. Planets here can show past lives as pilgrim, scholar or priest, and a strong pull toward certain cultures or ideas.
## Stories it may point to

People with planets here often describe a deep feeling for another country or culture, a love of languages or an old sense of faith. A challenged ninth house may point to old dogma, persecution for belief or lost faith.
## The lesson
To find your own truth and to hold it with an open mind. The work is meaning.
## Questions to sit with
* What do I believe, and why?
* Which place or culture feels like home to me?
* What do I want to understand?
hidden: The ninth house is linked with philosophy and the spiritual path. Many people with planets here are drawn to esoteric traditions, other cultures and the search for a bigger picture.
## In practice

People with planets in the ninth house often study comparative religion, astrology as philosophy, pilgrimage and the history of ideas. They tend to see practice as a path of understanding, and are natural teachers.

items.name: The Tenth House
basics: The tenth house is an angular house, one of the four corners of the chart, so planets here are strong and visible. It is linked with Capricorn and Saturn, which is its natural sign and ruler. It begins at the Midheaven, the highest point of the chart, and it is the most visible house.
## What it rules
Career, calling, public reputation, status, authority, achievement and your legacy.
## When it is strong
You have a clear sense of purpose and are drawn to leadership and achievement. Your reputation grows as you do.
## When it is a challenge
You may feel pressure to succeed, or unsure of your calling. You may be driven by status, or feel that your public role and private self do not match.
## Planets in this house
Planets here show your public role and your reputation. They are very visible and are often a clue to your vocation.
## The sign on this house

The sign on the edge of the house, called its cusp, colours how the area of life works for you, and the planet that rules that sign is called the house ruler. Follow it to the house it sits in to see how this area of life connects with the others. An empty house is not a weak one: it is simply read through its sign and its ruler.
past: The tenth house points to old roles in public life, such as rulers, leaders and teachers. It may show past authority or past shame, and a calling that you are growing into.
## Stories it may point to

People with planets here sometimes describe a strong sense of destiny, a feeling of having held authority before or a fear of public exposure. A challenged tenth house may point to old falls from status, or the weight of public responsibility.
## The lesson
To claim your calling with humility and integrity. The work is purpose.
## Questions to sit with
* What do I want to be known for?
* What does success mean to me?
* What would I do if I trusted my calling?

items.name: The Eleventh House
basics: The eleventh house is a succedent house, which follows an angular house and is about stabilising and building. It is linked with Aquarius, Uranus and Saturn, which is its natural sign and ruler. It is the house of the community you choose and the future you hope for.
## What it rules
Friends, groups, communities, causes, networks, hopes and wishes for the future.
## When it is strong
You have good friends and thrive in groups. You hold ideals, and you tend to attract allies and supporters.
## When it is a challenge
You may feel like an outsider, be disappointed by friends or groups, or find it hard to belong without losing yourself.
## Planets in this house
Planets here show the kind of friends and groups you are drawn to and what you hope for. They are often linked with community.
## The sign on this house

The sign on the edge of the house, called its cusp, colours how the area of life works for you, and the planet that rules that sign is called the house ruler. Follow it to the house it sits in to see how this area of life connects with the others. An empty house is not a weak one: it is simply read through its sign and its ruler.
past: The eleventh house points to old groups and fellowships, such as brotherhoods, circles and causes. It may show friends you have known across lives and the community you are meant to find.
## Stories it may point to

People with planets here often describe a sense of soul friends, of finding their people and of belonging to a certain circle. A challenged eleventh house may suggest old exile, betrayal by a group or the pain of not belonging.
## The lesson
To find your people, and to belong without conforming. The work is community.
## Questions to sit with
* Where do I feel I belong?
* What do I hope for?
* What does friendship ask of me?

items.name: The Twelfth House
basics: The twelfth house is a cadent house, which sits before an angular house and is about learning, adapting and preparing. It is linked with Pisces, Neptune and Jupiter, which is its natural sign and ruler. It is the last house, just before the Ascendant, and it holds what is hidden, ending and about to be reborn.
## What it rules
The subconscious, dreams, solitude, secrets, spirituality, retreat, hospitals and institutions, endings and what you cannot see in yourself.
## When it is strong
You have a rich inner life and deep intuition. You are compassionate, comfortable with solitude and able to sense what lies beneath.
## When it is a challenge
You may feel hidden or invisible, struggle with self sabotage, or be overwhelmed by what you absorb. It can be hard to name what you feel.
## Planets in this house
Planets here work behind the scenes. They are often subtle, private and hard to put into words, and they carry a sense of hidden depth.
## The sign on this house

The sign on the edge of the house, called its cusp, colours how the area of life works for you, and the planet that rules that sign is called the house ruler. Follow it to the house it sits in to see how this area of life connects with the others. An empty house is not a weak one: it is simply read through its sign and its ruler.
past: The twelfth house is the best known past-life house. It is read as what you carry unseen: old secrets, retreat, sacrifice and karma. Planets here suggest what you have not yet let go of.
## Stories it may point to

People with planets here often describe a deep inner world, a feeling of being haunted by something they cannot name, strong dreams or a need for solitude. A challenged twelfth house may suggest old confinement, convents, exile, secrets or sacrifice.
## The lesson
To forgive, to release and to bring what is hidden into the light at your own pace. The work is surrender, and trust.
## Questions to sit with
* What am I carrying that I cannot name?
* What do I need to release?
* How can I rest in the unseen?
hidden: The twelfth house is the house of the hidden. It is linked with intuition, dreams, mysticism and retreat, with working in secret, and with sensing what others cannot.
## In practice

People with planets in the twelfth house are often drawn to meditation, dreamwork, solitary practice and spiritual retreat. They may work best in private, and they often sense things before they have words for them. Protecting your energy and taking time to rest are especially important here.

items.name: The North Node
items.summary: The direction your growth points toward.
basics: The North Node is a point, not a planet. It is the place where the Moon's path crosses the Sun's path, and it moves backwards through the zodiac, taking about eighteen months to cross each sign and about eighteen and a half years to complete the circle. It always sits exactly opposite the South Node.

Together the two nodes are called the nodal axis. The North Node marks the direction of growth in this lifetime: what feels new, unfamiliar and a little awkward, and what you are becoming. It is a pull and not a pressure. Many people find it fits like a destination that they recognise when they arrive.
## What it governs
Your direction of growth, your purpose in this lifetime, the qualities you are developing and the experiences that stretch you.
## At its best
When you move towards your North Node, life tends to feel meaningful, even when it is hard. You grow, and you often feel more yourself.
## When it is hard
The North Node feels unfamiliar, so it is easy to avoid. Many people spend years in the comfort of the South Node before they turn. When you do, a certain amount of fear and clumsiness is normal.
## Finding it in your chart

The North Node glyph looks like a horseshoe opening downwards, with two small circles at its ends. Its sign and house show the direction of growth. Many astrology apps show both the North and the South Node, and some use the Mean Node and some the True Node. Either is fine to start with.
## The North Node through the signs
* Aries: You are growing towards courage, independence and leading your own life. You may feel awkward asserting yourself, and that is the point.
* Taurus: You are growing towards simplicity, stability and trusting your own worth. Slow down, rest and build something that is yours.
* Gemini: You are growing towards curiosity, questions and everyday connection. You are learning to hold ideas lightly and to listen.
* Cancer: You are growing towards feeling, care and creating a home. You are learning to be vulnerable and to nurture.
* Leo: You are growing towards joy, creativity and being seen. You are learning to trust your heart and to take up space.
* Virgo: You are growing towards service, discernment and practical skill. You are learning to bring your ideals down to earth.
* Libra: You are growing towards partnership, fairness and balance. You are learning to cooperate and to see another point of view.
* Scorpio: You are growing towards depth, honesty and transformation. You are learning to trust, to be intimate and to let go.
* Sagittarius: You are growing towards meaning, faith and wider horizons. You are learning to look up and to trust the bigger picture.
* Capricorn: You are growing towards responsibility, structure and a public purpose. You are learning to stand in your own authority.
* Aquarius: You are growing towards community, ideals and your own originality. You are learning to belong to something bigger than yourself.
* Pisces: You are growing towards compassion, intuition and surrender. You are learning to trust the unseen and to let go of control.
## The North Node through the houses
* 1st house: You are learning to put yourself first, to be independent and to know what you want.
* 2nd house: You are learning to build your own resources and to trust your worth.
* 3rd house: You are learning to ask questions, to communicate and to value what is close.
* 4th house: You are learning to build a home, to feel and to put down roots.
* 5th house: You are learning to play, to create and to take risks in love.
* 6th house: You are learning to serve, to build good habits and to care for your body.
* 7th house: You are learning to share, to compromise and to meet others as equals.
* 8th house: You are learning to trust, to share deeply and to face change.
* 9th house: You are learning to explore, to trust a bigger meaning and to teach.
* 10th house: You are learning to step into a public role and to follow a calling.
* 11th house: You are learning to belong to a group, to have friends and to hope.
* 12th house: You are learning to rest, to trust the unseen and to listen to your inner life.
past: The North Node is read as the lesson you came here to learn. It is the other half of the story told by the South Node: where the South Node shows what you already know, the North Node shows what you are here to develop.
## Stories it may point to

Many readers say the North Node feels like a distant memory of the future: something you feel drawn to long before you can explain why. It is rarely comfortable at first, because it asks you to do what you have not done before. The skills of the South Node are then used in service of the North.
People often describe a sense of coming alive when they act on their North Node, and a sense of being stuck or flat when they stay with the familiar.
## The lesson
Move towards the North Node a little at a time, and use the gifts of the South Node to get there. You do not have to leave your strengths behind.
## Questions to sit with
* What do I feel pulled towards that scares me a little?
* What would I try if I were not worried about doing it badly?
* What from my South Node could help me?

items.name: The South Node
items.summary: What you already know and carry with you.
basics: The South Node is the point exactly opposite the North Node. It is the place where the Moon's path crosses the Sun's path going south. It moves backwards through the zodiac, taking about eighteen months to cross each sign.

It shows what is familiar: your habits, talents and comfort zones. It is a strength that can become a rut. Many people feel at home with their South Node placements, and slightly bored or stuck when they stay with them too long.
## What it governs
Habits, inherited talents, comfort zones, what comes naturally and the patterns you return to under stress.
## At its best
The South Node is a source of natural skill and ease. You can use it as a resource while you grow towards the North Node, and you do not need to abandon what you are good at.
## When it is hard
Under stress, you may fall back on the South Node: the old reaction, the old role. It can feel safe, but it does not lead to growth.
## Finding it in your chart
The glyph is a horseshoe opening upwards, with two small circles at its ends. Find the North Node first, and the South Node is the sign and the house opposite.
past: The South Node is the best known of the past-life points. In this tradition it is read as skills you bring with you, the way you used to live, and the patterns you may be ready to loosen so that you can grow towards the North Node.
## Stories it may point to

Many people describe their South Node as the thing that comes easily, the role they slip into, or the familiar feeling of having done it before. Its sign suggests the kind of life it came from, and its house shows the area in which you carry the most experience.
It is not a debt or a punishment. It is a store of experience. The task is to use it with awareness, and not to be trapped by it.
## The South Node through the signs, with the North Node lesson
* Aries: You come with courage, independence and a habit of going it alone. You may fight first and think later. Growth lies towards cooperation and relationship.
* Taurus: You come with patience, comfort and a strong hold on what is yours. You may cling to security. Growth lies towards change, depth and shared resources.
* Gemini: You come with curiosity, quick wit and a gift for talking. You may scatter your energy and stay on the surface. Growth lies towards focus, truth and meaning.
* Cancer: You come with deep care, a strong feeling for family and emotional memory. You may hold on to the past. Growth lies towards your own authority and a life in the world.
* Leo: You come with charisma, creativity and the habit of being the centre. You may seek applause. Growth lies towards the group and shared purpose.
* Virgo: You come with skill, service and an eye for detail. You may over analyse and criticise yourself. Growth lies towards faith, intuition and letting go of control.
* Libra: You come with charm, diplomacy and a gift for partnership. You may lose yourself in others. Growth lies towards independence and trusting your own will.
* Scorpio: You come with intensity, psychological depth and survival instinct. You may hold on to control, secrets and old wounds. Growth lies towards trust, simplicity and letting life be.
* Sagittarius: You come with faith, adventure and a love of big truths. You may preach or run. Growth lies towards curiosity, listening and the details of everyday life.
* Capricorn: You come with discipline, authority and the habit of carrying responsibility alone. Growth lies towards feeling, nurturing and asking for support.
* Aquarius: You come with originality, detachment and a gift for the group. You may stand apart. Growth lies towards the heart, creativity and being personally seen.
* Pisces: You come with compassion, intuition and a habit of dissolving or escaping. Growth lies towards discernment, practical skill and clear boundaries.
## The South Node through the houses, with the North Node lesson
* 1st house: North Node in the 7th. A strong sense of self and independence from the past. Growth lies towards partnership and sharing the spotlight.
* 2nd house: North Node in the 8th. Familiar with your own resources and values. Growth lies towards shared resources, intimacy and letting go.
* 3rd house: North Node in the 9th. Familiar with everyday information and local life. Growth lies towards big truths, belief and wider horizons.
* 4th house: North Node in the 10th. Deeply tied to family, home and the past. Growth lies towards a public role and a purpose in the world.
* 5th house: North Node in the 11th. Familiar with the self, romance and being the star. Growth lies towards friends, groups and shared hopes.
* 6th house: North Node in the 12th. Familiar with work, service and routine. Growth lies towards faith, solitude and surrendering control.
* 7th house: North Node in the 1st. Familiar with partnership and living for others. Growth lies towards independence and a self of your own.
* 8th house: North Node in the 2nd. Familiar with intensity, shared power and crisis. Growth lies towards self worth, simplicity and building your own resources.
* 9th house: North Node in the 3rd. Familiar with belief, teaching and distant places. Growth lies towards curiosity, listening and the local and close at hand.
* 10th house: North Node in the 4th. Familiar with public roles and ambition. Growth lies towards home, family and your inner life.
* 11th house: North Node in the 5th. Familiar with groups and causes. Growth lies towards self expression, creativity and personal joy.
* 12th house: North Node in the 6th. Familiar with solitude, mysticism and retreat. Growth lies towards practical work, service and the everyday world.
## The lesson
To honour what you already know and to step beyond it. Many people find the South Node is the best teacher of the North, because the skills you already have are exactly what you need for the journey.
## Questions to sit with
* What comes so easily to me that I take it for granted?
* Which old role do I fall back on when I am afraid?
* What am I ready to put down?

items.name: Chiron
items.summary: The old wound and the gift it becomes.
basics: Chiron is a small body that orbits between Saturn and Uranus. It was discovered in 1977 and named after the wise centaur of Greek myth, who was wounded by a poisoned arrow and could not heal himself, yet became the teacher of healers. It takes about fifty years to circle the zodiac, spending anything from about two to eight years in a sign.

In a birth chart Chiron marks a sensitive place where you may have felt hurt, rejected or inadequate, and the healing skill that grows out of it. It is called the wounded healer because those who have known a pain closely are often the ones best able to help others with it.
## What it governs
Old wounds, sensitivity, healing, teaching, empathy, the places where you feel not good enough and the gifts that grow from them.
## At its best
A healed or healing Chiron brings real compassion. You become a gentle teacher, a skilled healer or simply a person others feel safe with.
## When it is hard
The wound can feel tender and permanent. It may show up as shame, self criticism, or a belief that this one thing will never change. Healing is more often a gradual acceptance than a cure.
## Finding it in your chart

The glyph is a key, or a circle with a line rising from it. Its sign shows the nature of the wound and the gift, and its house shows where it is most felt. Chiron returns to its birth position at about age 50, which is often a time of deeper acceptance.
## Chiron through the signs
* Aries: The wound is about identity and the right to exist and assert yourself. The gift is courage and the ability to help others find theirs.
* Taurus: The wound is about worth, security and the body. The gift is a grounded presence and the power to help others feel safe.
* Gemini: The wound is about being heard or understood. The gift is communication that heals.
* Cancer: The wound is about belonging, nurture and family. The gift is deep emotional care.
* Leo: The wound is about being seen and loved for who you are. The gift is the confidence to bring joy to others.
* Virgo: The wound is about not being good enough or perfect. The gift is practical healing and service.
* Libra: The wound is about relationship and fairness. The gift is the ability to help others find balance.
* Scorpio: The wound is about trust, power and intimacy. The gift is the power to transform pain.
* Sagittarius: The wound is about meaning and faith. The gift is teaching and inspiring others.
* Capricorn: The wound is about authority, success and responsibility. The gift is the ability to guide others with integrity.
* Aquarius: The wound is about being different and not belonging. The gift is acceptance of difference and a gift for community.
* Pisces: The wound is about boundaries and feeling too much. The gift is compassion and spiritual healing.
## Chiron through the houses
* 1st house: A wound around identity and self image. You may feel awkward in your own skin, and you grow into authenticity.
* 2nd house: A wound around worth and money. You learn to value yourself.
* 3rd house: A wound around speech, learning or siblings. You may heal through writing and teaching.
* 4th house: A wound around family and home. You learn to make your own safe place.
* 5th house: A wound around joy, love and creativity. You learn to play and to be open in love.
* 6th house: A wound around work and health. You may heal through helping and caring for others.
* 7th house: A wound around partnership. You learn how to relate and to choose well.
* 8th house: A wound around trust, intimacy and loss. You may become a guide through transformation.
* 9th house: A wound around belief and meaning. You grow into a teacher of your own truth.
* 10th house: A wound around ambition and public life. You learn to claim your calling.
* 11th house: A wound around belonging and friendship. You find your place among others who are different.
* 12th house: A hidden wound, often not understood. Healing comes through solitude, compassion and spiritual practice.
past: Chiron is read as a wound that goes back further than this life: an old hurt that returns until it is understood. In past-life astrology it is the sensitive spot that you may have carried across lifetimes.
## Stories it may point to

Chiron is linked to experiences of rejection, injury or being unable to help yourself or others. A person with a strong Chiron may feel they have been trying to heal one particular thing for a very long time. They often describe sensitivity that has no clear source in this life.

But Chiron is also the teacher. In the same stories, the pain becomes the doorway to healing others. Many people with a prominent Chiron find that the thing that hurt them most is exactly what they are most able to help with.
## The lesson
To meet the wound with compassion, and to understand that healing does not mean the pain vanishes. It means it no longer rules you.
## Questions to sit with
* What hurts that I have never been able to fix?
* How has it made me able to help others?
* What would acceptance feel like?
hidden: Chiron is the wounded healer. In the hidden chart he is linked with the healing arts, from herbs and energy work to counselling and ritual, and with a gift for guiding others through pain that you know well.
## In practice

People with a prominent Chiron often become healers, teachers, herbalists, tarot readers or listeners of some kind, drawn to the work because of their own experience. A grounded practice and good boundaries matter, because the wound can resonate with the pain of others.

items.name: Black Moon Lilith
items.summary: The wild part you were told to hide.
basics: Black Moon Lilith is a calculated point, not a planet. It is usually taken to be the Moon's farthest point from Earth, called the lunar apogee, and astrologers calculate it in more than one way. It is not the asteroid Lilith, and the name comes from the figure of Lilith in Jewish folklore, the first woman, who refused to submit. It spends about nine months in each sign.

In modern astrology it stands for the raw, instinctive part of you that refuses to be tamed: your wildness, your anger, your sexuality, your no. It is often described as the part of you that was told to be quiet, or that you learned to hide in order to belong.
## What it governs
Raw instinct, rebellion, anger, sexuality, the refusal to conform, the shadow, what has been rejected or shamed and the power in reclaiming it.
## At its best
When you own your Lilith, you are free, honest and powerful, and no longer ruled by what other people want you to be. You can set boundaries without apology.
## When it is hard
A buried Lilith can appear as shame, rage, secret desires, or relationships built around being seen only partly. Reclaiming it takes patience and care.
## Finding it in your chart

There is no official glyph, and most charts show a small black moon with a cross. Not every chart program shows it, so you may need to turn it on. Its sign shows how your wildness expresses itself, and its house shows where you feel most unbound or most judged.
past: Lilith is read as a memory of being silenced, shamed or cast out, and of power that was feared. In past-life astrology, her sign and house show where the old wound of not belonging is still tender, and where your freedom lies.
## Stories it may point to

Many people read Lilith as lives as the outsider: the one who was exiled, burned, locked away or misunderstood for being too strong, too sexual, too wild or too knowing. Others link her to the part of themselves they hid in order to survive.
This does not have to be literal. It describes a quality of experience: the rawness of having been punished for something natural. The gift on the other side is a great deal of power and honesty.
## The lesson
To reclaim what was rejected, and to be who you are without apology, while keeping yourself safe.
## Questions to sit with
* What part of me was I told to hide?
* When do I feel most wild and most free?
* Where do I still say yes when I mean no?
hidden: Lilith is the witchy point. She is linked with the outsider, the rebel and the wise woman who lives at the edge of the village, and with taking back what you were told to hide.
## In practice

People with a prominent Lilith are often drawn to shadow work, to the old stories of women and witches, and to rituals of reclaiming: speaking your no aloud, writing a letter to the part of you that was silenced, or marking a boundary. She rewards honesty and does not respond well to pretending.

guides.title: How To Read Your Own Birth Chart
guides.summary: A gentle step by step way to read your chart, with no maths.

ps: Every part of a birth chart is built from three things: a planet, a sign and a house. Once you know what each one does, you can read almost any placement.
The planet is what is happening: the energy or part of you. The sign is how it happens: the style and the flavour. The house is where it happens: the area of life.

So Venus in Leo in the fifth house reads like this. Venus is love and what you value. Leo is the style, warm, proud and generous. The fifth house is the area, creativity, romance and play. Together they say: you love openly and generously, and you come alive through creative joy.
Use the Planets, Signs and Houses pages in this section to look up each part as you go.
This app does not calculate charts. To read your own, you first need a chart, and many astrology websites and apps will make one for free.
You will need the date, the time and the place of your birth. The Rising sign and the houses depend on the time, so try to find your birth time on your birth certificate or ask a family member.
If you do not know your time, you can still read your planets by sign. Leave the houses and the Rising sign for later.
Begin with your Sun, Moon and Rising signs. They give you a first picture without much work.
The Sun is your core self and what you are growing into. The Moon is your feelings and what you need to feel safe. The Rising sign is the face you show the world and the way you begin things.
Write one sentence for each, then read them together. Notice where they agree and where they pull in different directions. That tension is part of what makes you interesting.
The twelve houses are twelve areas of life, from you and your money to your career, friends and the hidden parts of your life. Your Rising sign sets where the first house begins.

Look to see which houses hold your planets. A house with several planets is a busy area of your life. A house with none is not unimportant. It is simply less in the spotlight, and you can read it through the sign on its edge and the planet that rules that sign.
The Houses pages in this section describe each one.

Before you look at single placements, step back and look at the balance of the whole chart. The twelve signs fall into four elements and three modes, and counting where your planets sit gives you a quick feel for your temperament.
## The four elements
* Fire (Aries, Leo, Sagittarius): Energy, enthusiasm, courage and inspiration. Too little and you may lack drive. Too much and you may burn out.
* Earth (Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn): Practicality, patience, the senses and steady effort. Too little and you may struggle to ground things. Too much and you may resist change.
* Air (Gemini, Libra, Aquarius): Thought, communication, ideas and connection. Too little and you may struggle to put things into words. Too much and you may live in your head.
* Water (Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces): Feeling, intuition, empathy and depth. Too little and you may feel cut off from emotion. Too much and you may feel overwhelmed.
## The three modes
* Cardinal (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn): The starters. They begin things and set direction.
* Fixed (Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius): The sustainers. They hold steady, commit and resist change.
* Mutable (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces): The adapters. They adjust, refine and finish things.
Count your ten planets, plus the Rising sign, and see which element and mode appear most. It is a simple way to find the character of your chart, and a good place to begin.

Sometimes a planet appears to move backwards through the zodiac, as seen from Earth. This is an optical effect, and it is called retrograde. Your chart will mark retrograde planets with an R, or a symbol that looks like Rx.

A retrograde planet in your birth chart is traditionally read as one whose energy works inwardly or in a more reflective, unusual way. Mercury retrograde, for example, may think more slowly and deeply, and go back over things. In past-life astrology, retrograde planets are often read as unfinished business.
It does not make a planet weaker. It makes it more personal and more internal, and often it takes a little longer to find its voice.
Aspects are the angles between planets. They show how two parts of you work together.
A conjunction is a blend. A sextile is an easy opportunity. A trine is a natural flow. A square is friction that makes you act. An opposition is a pull between two sides that asks for balance.
You do not need to learn every aspect at once. Start with the ones that involve your Sun, Moon or Rising, and the tightest ones, where the planets are within a few degrees.

When you are ready to read a whole chart, work in this order. First, your Sun, Moon and Rising. Second, the ruler of your Rising sign, which is a key planet in your chart. Third, each planet by sign and house. Fourth, the closest aspects. Fifth, the nodes and Chiron, for the deeper story.
Write a short paragraph at each step, in your own words. At the end, read your paragraphs through. That is your first reading, and it will get richer each time you come back.
A chart shows tendencies and themes, not fixed outcomes. You always have a choice about how to use what you find.
Do not read your Sun sign alone. It is only one part of a whole picture.
Be patient. Astrology is a language, and it takes time. Look up one placement a day and let the meanings settle.

guides.title: Past-Life Astrology: How To Use This Section
guides.summary: What the tradition says, and how to use it well.

ps: Past-life astrology reads the birth chart as a record of the soul's story as well as of this life. It asks what patterns, gifts and unfinished lessons you may have brought with you.

It belongs to a long line of ideas about the soul moving through many lives, which we studied in the first cycle of the Archive. In its modern form it developed in the twentieth century, and many astrologers now work with it.

It is a tradition and a lens for reflection. It is not a proven fact, and it does not need to be literal to be useful. Many people find that the stories it suggests help them understand their own patterns.

pages.h: Where To Look In The Chart
ps: The best known indicators are the South Node, which shows what you bring with you, and the North Node, which shows where you are growing. Saturn shows lessons and old responsibilities, and Pluto the deepest layers of power and change. Chiron shows the old wound and the healing gift.

The Fourth, Eighth and Twelfth Houses are often read as the houses of the past, and of what is hidden. Planets that were retrograde at birth are sometimes read as pointing to unfinished business from earlier in the soul's story.
Use the Planets, Points, Signs and Houses pages here and open the Past lives view on each.

The nodes are the heart of most past-life astrology, so it is worth spending time with them. The South Node is what you bring: your talents, habits and ease. The North Node is where you are headed, and it feels new and a little uncomfortable.

A helpful way to read them is as a pair. Look up your South Node and your North Node together, and notice the movement from one to the other. The aim is not to abandon the South Node but to use its skills in the service of the North.
Open the South Node page to see each sign and house, with the matching North Node lesson.

Some astrologers read retrograde planets in the birth chart as themes that are being revisited, or lessons that were not finished. A retrograde Saturn, for example, might suggest that the work of responsibility or authority carries on from before, while a retrograde Venus might suggest unfinished lessons in love and self worth.
This is one interpretation among many, and it works best as a question and not a verdict. If you have retrograde planets, you might ask what that area of life is asking you to look at again.
Pick one placement, such as your South Node or Saturn. Read its past-life page slowly. Then write for ten minutes in answer to one of the questions at the bottom.
Do not edit or judge what comes. Notice images, feelings and memories, and anything that surprises you. Come back a week later and see what still feels true.
Over a few weeks you will begin to see patterns, and that is where the real value of this work lies.
Treat each reading as a question and not an answer. Ask yourself whether it rings true, and what it would mean if it did.
Write it down. A journal is the best partner for this work. Over time, notice which themes keep returning.

Never let a past-life story excuse harm, or replace a choice you can make now. The point of the lens is to understand a pattern so that you can change it. If a theme brings up pain you cannot manage, please speak to a doctor or a therapist you trust.

guides.title: The Hidden Chart: Occult And Witchy Placements
guides.summary: The placements astrologers link with the unusual, the mystical and the magical.

ps: Some placements are traditionally linked with an interest in the hidden, the mystical and the magical. This part of the section brings them together in one place.

It is a game of resonance and not of rules. Plenty of people with these placements have no interest in the occult, and plenty of people drawn to it have chart patterns that look nothing like these. Use it as a prompt for curiosity.

The Eighth and Twelfth Houses are the houses of the unseen. Scorpio and Pisces are the signs most often linked with mystery and intuition. Pluto and Neptune are the planets of the depths and of the veil, and the Moon is the planet of dreams and instinct.
Uranus and Aquarius are linked with the unusual and with astrology itself. Chiron is the wounded healer, and Black Moon Lilith is the witchy outsider.
Open the Hidden chart view on each of these pages to read more.

One placement means little on its own. The hidden chart is a pattern, so look for several signs pointing the same way: a Scorpio Moon, a Pluto in the eighth house, a prominent Neptune, planets in the twelfth.

Then look at the practical side. Which of these placements have you actually felt in your life? Which parts of the occult world have you been curious about, and which have you been drawn to without being sure why?
Use the Hidden chart view on each page to read more, and write down what rings true.

pages.h: Reading It With A Clear Head
ps: A strong pull toward the unseen goes best with grounding. Eat, sleep, spend time outdoors and keep your friendships.

If you have visions, voices or experiences that frighten you, or that you cannot step back from, please talk to a doctor or someone you trust. Curiosity about the mystical is healthy, and so is asking for help.
